title: Combat
desc: Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival.
text: Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-of-turn and end-of-turn timing is literal. Reactions follow their trigger wording and are not inserted retroactively after the consequence has already resolved unless a rule explicitly allows it. Movement, Positioning & Physical Interaction Ground Movement Base Walk. 30 feet for a Daeva unless modified. Difficult Terrain. Costs 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot traveled. Prone. Standing from Prone requires one full Action and does not consume movement. A creature can move normally afterward if movement remains available. No universal Flanking. Opposite sides do not automatically grant Advantage. No universal Facing. Being behind a creature does not automatically grant Advantage. Occupied Spaces. A creature may move through a willing allied creature's space, treating that space as difficult terrain unless an explicit feature says otherwise. A creature cannot move through an enemy or neutral creature's occupied space unless an explicit rule permits it, and cannot end movement in another creature's occupied space unless an explicit rule allows it. Grapple and Shove Grapple and Shove each require a full Action. The target must be within reach and no more than one Size larger than you. Make Strength (Athletics) contested by the target’s choice of Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). On a successful Grapple, the target becomes Grappled; it may use its Action to escape by repeating the contest. Moving a Grappled creature costs 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot moved unless the target is at least two Sizes smaller than you. On a successful Shove, choose to push the target 5 feet or knock it Prone. Grapple and Shove do not replace attacks within the Attack Action and cannot substitute for Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. Player characters do not use a universal Unarmed Attack damage rule; the normal Attack Action requires an approved class weapon unless an explicit feature says otherwise. Disarm Disarm is a full Action. The attacker uses Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), contested by the defender’s Strength (Athletics)

title: Concentration
desc: Concentration does not use checks or saving throws as a general mechanic. A creature can maintain only one Concentration effect at a time. Beginning another Concentration effect immediately ends the previous one. Damage, attacks, forced movement, falling, and similar events do not test Concentration. Concentration ends when the creature becomes Incapacitated
text: Concentration Concentration does not use checks or saving throws as a general mechanic. A creature can maintain only one Concentration effect at a time. Beginning another Concentration effect immediately ends the previous one. Damage, attacks, forced movement, falling, and similar events do not test Concentration. Concentration ends when the creature becomes Incapacitated, voluntarily ends it, begins another Concentration effect, or an explicit rule says the Concentration ends.

text: Consumables, Professions & Economy Player Rules Professions & Economy Consumables, Kinah, Profession training, supplies, production, upgrades, Alchemy, and Cooking. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Consumables, Professions & Economy Currency Professions Training Profession Supplies Facilities and Work Weaponsmithing Armorcrafting Consumables, Professions & Economy Currency Kinah is the only universal currency. WoA does not use denominations. Professions Wings of Atreia uses five Professions: Weaponsmithing, Armorcrafting, Handicrafting, Alchemy, and Cooking. A character may have only one Active Profession at a time. The only Profession ranks are Apprentice and Master. There is no Profession XP, no intermediate rank, and no separate recipe, formula-book, manual, or recipe-learning subsystem. Earning a rank automatically grants the standard functions assigned to that rank. Rule Profession Ruling Starting Rank None. Backgrounds, including Artisan, grant no Profession rank. Active Limit One Active Profession at a time. Changing Profession Only when the character gains a character level. Inactive Profession Retains earned rank, paid entry fee, and completed Training Progress, but cannot be used or advanced. Reactivation Restores the highest earned rank and retained Training Progress; an already-paid rank entry fee is not paid again. Normal Work Checks No roll is required when all listed requirements are met. Training Rank Entry Fee Training Qualified Trainer Other Requirement Apprentice 100 Kinah 3 full Training Days Apprentice or Master in the same Profession None Master 500 Kinah 5 additional full Training Days Master in the same Profession Level 10+ and already Apprentice A Training Day is one exclusive full in-game day. The trainee and trainer cannot adventure, undertake missions, perform adventuring travel, conduct other downtime work, perform Profession production, or complete other substantive activities that day. Training Days need not be consecutive. An interrupted day grants no Training Progress, but previously completed Training Days remain. A character cannot train themselves. One qualified trainer may instruct up to four trainees of the same rank category during one Training Day. When a PC provides training, that PC receives the one-time entry fee: 100 Kinah per Apprentice trainee or 500 Kinah per Master trainee. NPC or institutional fees go to that provider. Profession Supplies Only Basic and Advanced supply grades exist mechanically. Specific ore, alloy, herb, spice, monster-part, crystal, reagent, or regional names are flavor only and do not change grade, quantity, value, or effect. Supply Basic Advanced Weapon Material 100 Kinah 300 Kinah Armor Material 100 Kinah 300 Kinah Handicraft Material 100 Kinah 300 Kinah Alchemical Reagent 25 Kinah 100 Kinah Cooking Ingredient 10 Kinah 50 Kinah Daily Merchant Stock. For each Basic Profession supply type a merchant carries, roll 1d8 once for that current in-game day. For an Advanced supply type, the GM first decides whether that merchant has Advanced stock at all. If not, stock is 0 and no roll is made; if yes, roll 1d4 once for that day. Roll separately for each supply type. Purchases reduce remaining stock; returning to the shop does not reroll it. Profession supplies may also enter play through missions, exploration, salvage, encounters, or NPC/faction rewards. There is no Gathering Profession and no default harvesting roll. Supply categories cannot substitute for one another. Facilities and Work Profession Required Facility Weaponsmithing Functional forge / weapon-working station Armorcrafting Functional armor-working forge/workshop Handicrafting Functional precision artisan / Implement workshop Alchemy Functional alchemical workbench/laboratory Cooking Functional kitchen or suitable camp-cooking station There are no facility quality tiers. Facility access fees, when any apply, are determined by the GM or the fiction. Weaponsmithing, Armorcrafting, and Handicrafting each require one exclusive full Profession Work Day per upgrade stage. If interrupted, the upgrade is incomplete, materials are not lost, and another full Work Day is required. Materials are consumed only when the work is successfully completed. Weaponsmithing Weaponsmithing upgrades an existing eligible Weapon obtained through the normal equipment-acquisition rules; it does not craft Weapons from scratch. Upgrade Rank Materials Time Result Common -> Profession +1 Apprentice 2 Basic Weapon Materials 1 Work Day +1 to Hit Profession +1 -> Profession +2 Master 2 Advanced Weapon Materials 1 Work Day +2 to Hit Upgrades are sequential. Weaponsmithing changes only the approved quality bonus; it does not change damage dice, damage type, weapon properties, reload/firing rules, class eligibility, Critical Edge, or other weapon traits. Armorcrafting Armorcrafting upgrades an existing eligible Armor item; it does not craft Armor from scratch and never upgrades Shields. Upgrade Rank Materials Time Result Common -> Profession +1 Apprentice 2 Basic Armor Materials 1 Work Day +1 AC Profession +1 -> Profession +2 Master 2 Advanced Armor Materials 1 Work Day +2 AC Armorcrafting does not change armor category, proficiency requirements, base AC formula, add Damage Reduction, add resistance, or add unrelated properties. Handicrafting Handicrafting upgrades an existing eligible Implement; it does not craft Implements from scratch and does not change an Implement's approved identity or special mechanics. Upgrade Rank Materials Time Result Common -> Profession +1 Apprentice 2 Basic Handicraft Materials 1 Work Day +1 Spell Attack Profession +1 -> Profession +2 Master 2 Advanced Handicraft Materials 1 Work Day +2 Spell Attack Alchemy Alchemy produces approved recovery and treatment consumables. Preparation requires 1 hour per consumable. If interrupted, no product is created and reagents are not consumed; reagents are consumed only when preparation is successfully completed. Aether Cure remains an NPC-purchased special consumable only and is not an Alchemy formula. text: Core / Eye of Reshanta The Core, also called the Eye of Reshanta, occupies the central strategic heart of the Abyss between Elysea and Asmodae. It is the most symbolically and militarily charged part of Reshanta, centered on the Divine Fortress and the central Balaur order that holds the starting-era position. Tower remnants and the immense broken interior of Atreia dominate the surrounding sense of scale. Reaching the Core means moving toward the center of a war that has endured for centuries. Neither Elyos nor Asmodians can treat the Core as ordinary homeland territory, and operations here carry consequences far beyond a single patrol. Balaur power, fortress strategy, aerial approaches, and the ambitions of both Daeva factions converge around the Eye. Player actions may eventually change the balance, because the starting map establishes a beginning rather than a protected future. The Core should feel like a place where tactical success can become history.

text: Core Engine — Resolve Resolve represents the Templar converting battlefield pressure into defensive certainty. Unless a later feature states otherwise, Resolve becomes 0 when Initiative is rolled, becomes 0 when combat ends, and cannot be gained while you are Incapacitated. Hold the Line: gain 1 Resolve when a hostile creature you can see hits you with an attack while you are within that creature’s melee reach. Protect the Vulnerable: gain 1 Resolve when a Templar class feature successfully reduces, prevents, redirects, or intercepts damage that would otherwise be dealt to another creature, or when a feature explicitly says the protection qualifies. You can normally gain no more than 1 Resolve during any creature’s turn. One event grants Resolve only once even if it satisfies multiple triggers. title: Core Resolution
desc: The d20 test framework used for meaningful uncertain outcomes.
text: Player Rules Core Resolution The d20 test framework used for meaningful uncertain outcomes. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks Saving Throws Save DCs Advantage and Disadvantage Help Passive Perception, Passive Investigation & Search d20 Tests & Core Resolution d20 Tests Ability Checks, attack rolls, and saving throws use a d20. Roll only when the outcome is uncertain and meaningful. If success is automatic, impossible, or consequence-free, no roll is needed. Ability Checks Choose the ability that best fits the approach, then add Proficiency Bonus if the character is proficient in the relevant skill. Expertise doubles the PB contribution for that proficiency. WoA retains six abilities and eighteen skills. A specialized Background can authorize a character to attempt obscure knowledge, but it does not automatically modify the roll. Saving Throws A saving throw uses the specified ability modifier and adds PB only if the creature is proficient in that saving throw. Ties are resolved according to the specific system; otherwise meeting a DC succeeds. Save DCs Default effect Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + the relevant ability modifier, unless an explicit class, spell, item, monster, or environmental rule gives a different DC. text: Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself.

text: d20 Tests, Actions & Combat Are natural 1 and natural 20 automatic on every d20 Test? No. Ability Checks and Saving Throws compare the final total to the DC. Attack rolls keep their explicit natural-1 automatic miss and natural-20 automatic hit/critical rules. How does Help work? A meaningful helper gives +2 to one Ability Check . Help does not grant Advantage. There is no Assist Attack, and Help does not modify Death Saves. Can Grapple or Shove replace one attack from Extra Attack? No. Grapple and Shove are each a full Action . How do I stand from Prone? Standing from Prone requires your full Action and consumes no movement. Does flanking automatically grant Advantage? No. Wings of Atreia has no universal Flanking rule and no universal Facing rule. Is there a Surprise Round? No. In a genuine ambush, the GM may allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack. That is discretionary and is not an extra round. How is 3D distance measured? When horizontal and vertical separation both matter, use the greater of the two distances rather than adding them. Does taking damage at 0 HP automatically add failed Death Saves? No. Ordinary damage while already at 0 HP does not alter the Death Save track. A natural 1 on a Death Save is exactly one failure.

text: Daeva Points & Ultimate Abilities LEVEL 10 UNIVERSAL FEATURE. Beginning at Level 10, a Daeva can accumulate up to 100 Daeva Points (DP). At 100 DP, the Daeva's class Ultimate Ability is ready and may be attempted. A successful Ultimate attack expends all 100 DP. If the Ultimate attack misses, the player chooses Release the Power or Hold the Power after the miss is confirmed, as described below. Earning DP. At the end of genuine combat, the GM totals the DP values of eligible hostile creatures defeated in that combat. Every Level 10 or higher Daeva who meaningfully participated gains that full total; the award is not divided and never depends on the killing blow. DP is awarded only after combat has fully ended, so DP gained from a victory cannot ready another Ultimate during that same combat. Enemy Rank / Significance DP Award No eligible threat / trivial opposition 0 DP Standard 2 DP Veteran 3 DP Elite 5 DP Boss 10 DP Climactic Boss 20 DP Climactic Boss. Climactic Boss is a DP-award designation, not a new Monster Compendium Rank. The GM may use it for a Boss that serves as the decisive threat of a major story arc; an ordinary Boss remains worth 10 DP. Eligible Defeat. A hostile creature counts when the party overcomes it through genuine combat, whether it is killed, reduced to 0 HP, captured, forced to surrender, or decisively driven from the encounter. Training, sparring, staged encounters, deliberately farmed enemies, allied or controlled creatures, summoned creatures, repeated forms of the same creature, and opposition that never represented a genuine threat award 0 DP. The GM makes the final eligibility ruling. Persistence and Restrictions. DP persists between encounters and through Short Rests, Long Rests, and Aetheric Reconstitution. Resting, consumables, spells, equipment, and class-resource effects cannot grant or restore DP. DP cannot exceed 100, be transferred, have its cost reduced, or be spent for any purpose other than the character's class Ultimate unless a future rule explicitly says otherwise. A character below Level 10 cannot earn or bank DP. Warfront Exclusion. DP cannot be gained or spent and Ultimate Abilities cannot be activated during a Warfront operation. This includes character-scale missions embedded in that operation and the Fortress Core Brigadier-General encounter. A character retains existing DP while the Warfront is in progress. Ultimate Attack Roll. Activating an Ultimate consumes both the character's Action and Bonus Action. The character cannot activate it unless both are available, but may still move and take Reactions normally. When the Ultimate requires an attack roll, roll 1d20 + the applicable ability modifier + the character's Proficiency Bonus, with Advantage. Advantage and Disadvantage interact normally, and other explicit modifiers apply normally. The attack is not an Attack action and cannot be duplicated by Extra Attack, Quick Shot, Akimbo, additional-action effects, reactions, or similar features. Fixed Ultimate Output, Miss Choice, and Critical Hits. Damage or healing dice printed as the Ultimate's own direct numerical output are not rolled; use the maximum value of those dice. Normal weapon or Bastion weapon damage and damage dice from other features remain rolled normally. On a hit, resolve normal weapon/Bastion damage when applicable, all fixed Ultimate damage or healing, and the Ultimate's full legal riders, then expend all 100 DP. On a miss, normal weapon/Bastion damage and full-hit riders do not occur. After the miss is confirmed, the player chooses one resolution. Release the Power: expend all 100 DP and resolve one-half, rounded down, of the Ultimate's fixed primary damage and one-half of any direct Ultimate healing, restoration, or repair amount that would have occurred on a hit. Area or secondary-target damage, temporary HP or other protective effects, forced movement, condition or status effects, condition removal, and other riders do not occur. If a restoration or repair sets a target to an HP threshold rather than rolling dice, determine how much HP the full hit would have restored from the target's current state and restore half that amount, rounded down. Hold the Power: resolve no Ultimate damage, healing, restoration, repair, or other effect and retain all 100 DP, but that Ultimate cannot be attempted again until the next dawn. Short Rests, Long Rests, and Aetheric Reconstitution do not end this restriction early. A critical hit does not increase fixed Ultimate output; only rolled normal weapon/Bastion damage dice double under the normal critical-hit rule. Resistance, Immunity, Vulnerability, and damage reduction apply normally. Ultimate Recovery and Rules Identity. Regardless of whether the Ultimate hits or which miss option is chosen, after the Ultimate attempt resolves the character's next turn is an Ultimate Recovery turn. During that turn, the character cannot make weapon attacks or spell attacks, deal damage, restore Hit Points, or impose conditions or harmful status effects on enemies. The character may move or fly normally, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Search, Use Object, provide Help or other non-healing aid, interact with objects or the environment, and use other legal non-offensive utility or defensive options that do not violate those restrictions. Reactions are unaffected and function normally, including Opportunity Attacks. Ultimate Recovery ends at the end of that turn. An Ultimate remains a class feature, not a spell, class resource, Attack action, or ordinary Bastion system; it does not consume ammunition, a spell use, a cooldown use, or another class resource unless its text explicitly says so. Ordinary on-hit riders apply only when their own triggers are satisfied, and no effect can repeat the Ultimate or multiply its fixed output. Use the Ultimate values for the character's current class-level band: Levels 10-14, Levels 15-19, or Level 20. ← Back to Rules

Does only the character who lands the killing blow gain DP? No. Eligible Level 10+ Daevas who meaningfully participated receive the full qualifying post-combat DP award; it is
text: Daeva Points & Ultimates When do I gain Daeva Points and unlock my Ultimate? Beginning at Level 10 , eligible Daevas can earn DP from genuine combat. Maximum DP is 100. At 100 DP, the class Ultimate is ready. Does only the character who lands the killing blow gain DP? No. Eligible Level 10+ Daevas who meaningfully participated receive the full qualifying post-combat DP award; it is not divided by killing blows. What happens when my Ultimate attack misses? After the miss is confirmed, the player chooses one of two final resolutions: Release the Power: spend all 100 DP and resolve one-half, rounded down, of the Ultimate's fixed primary damage plus one-half of any direct Ultimate healing, restoration, or repair amount that would have occurred on a hit. Normal weapon/Bastion damage, area or secondary-target damage, temporary HP/protection, forced movement, conditions/status effects, condition removal, and other riders do not occur. There is no next-dawn lockout . Hold the Power: resolve no Ultimate effect, retain all 100 DP, and that Ultimate cannot be attempted again until the next dawn. Rests and Aetheric Reconstitution do not end the lockout early. Ultimate Recovery occurs after either choice. What happens after an Ultimate attempt? Your next turn is an Ultimate Recovery turn whether the Ultimate hit, used Release the Power, or used Hold the Power. During that turn you cannot make weapon or spell attacks, deal damage, restore HP, or impose hostile conditions/status effects. You may still use legal movement, defensive, utility, environmental, and non-healing aid options. Reactions remain available, including Opportunity Attacks. Recovery ends at the end of that turn. Does a critical hit increase an Ultimate's fixed output? No. Fixed Ultimate output is not increased by the critical hit. Only rolled normal weapon/Bastion damage dice double when applicable. Can resting, equipment, consumables, or class features restore DP? No. DP persists through rests and Aetheric Reconstitution but is not restored by those systems. DP cannot exceed 100, be transferred, or have the 100-DP Ultimate cost reduced.

desc: Elysea forms the southern half of shattered Atreia and is the homeland of the Elyos. text: Elysea Elysea forms the southern half of shattered Atreia and is the homeland of the Elyos. Its regions range from fertile countryside and monumental cities to arid badlands, mountain forests, devastated islands, and places where ancient history remains close to the surface. Sanctum Sanctum is the monumental floating capital of Elysea, suspended above Oriel and visible as one of the great symbols of Elyos civilization. Its luminous plazas, temples, government halls, Legion offices, archives, and scholarly institutions make it a center of civic life as much as military power. The city was raised during the long southern reconstruction after the Cataclysm rather than surviving unchanged from ancient Atreia. Public ceremony, learning, art, diplomacy, and service all contribute to the capital’s cultivated identity. For Elyos Daevas, Sanctum is where victories become policy, discoveries enter archives, and service to Elysea can draw the attention of powerful institutions. Most civic areas are orderly and accessible, while military compounds, temple spaces, and restricted records remain controlled. Adventures here tend toward investigation, diplomacy, political consequences, research, or threats hidden beneath the security of the capital. Sanctum represents what Elyos society believes it rebuilt from the ruin of the old world. Oriel Oriel is the cultivated residential sanctuary directly beneath Sanctum on the same greater floating geography, not a distant island of its own. Gardens, estates, homes, workshops, and carefully maintained public spaces give it a gentler character than the monumental capital overhead. It reflects the domestic side of Elyos civilization: households, artistry, hospitality, and the patient work of maintaining a beautiful place to live. Its closeness to Sanctum ties everyday life directly to the political and religious heart of Elysea. Daevas who come to Oriel encounter the lives that continue beyond military service—families, artisans, residents, visitors, and generations shaped by an immortal society. The region can host social stories, community problems, personal obligations, celebrations, quiet investigations, and consequences that feel very different from fortress warfare. Its tranquility should not make it meaningless; Oriel helps show players what Elyos characters are actually protecting. Looking upward toward Sanctum also reinforces the intimate relationship between capital and home. Poeta Poeta is a fertile rural region of Elysea, defined by broad plains, farms, forests, and clear lakes. Akarios Village stands among a landscape that includes Cliona Lake, Daminu Forest, Kabarah Strip Mine, and Timolia Mine. Compared with the grandeur of Sanctum, Poeta feels close to the land and to the ordinary rhythms of food, work, family, and local community. Its pastoral appearance makes it one of the clearest expressions of the hospitable southern environment. For many Elyos, Poeta represents homeland in its most immediate form: fields worth tending, communities worth defending, and wilderness that still holds mysteries of its own. Daevas may be called to protect travelers, investigate trouble around mines and forests, assist isolated settlements, or deal with dangers that ordinary residents cannot face alone. The region works especially well for adventures where local stakes matter before the campaign expands into larger wars. Poeta reminds heroes that the fate of Atreia is ultimately measured in the lives that survive its conflicts. Verteron Verteron is a temperate defensive frontier where plains, coastline, woodland, roads, and old ruins meet. Verteron Citadel anchors the region alongside Tolbas Village, Verteron Observatory, Cantas Coast, Tursin Garrison, Zumion Ruins, and the road leading toward Eltnen. Its settled routes are never entirely removed from military vigilance, giving the region the feel of civilization pressed against contested ground. Ancient remains and active defenses stand side by side across the landscape. Service in Verteron emphasizes readiness, patrols, escort duty, reconnaissance, and the defense of communities that live close to danger. Daevas can move from a village problem to a ruined site or hostile position without leaving the region’s broader defensive story. The coexistence of roads, settlements, ruins, and enemy activity makes Verteron a natural place for exploration and field missions. It is a reminder that Elysea’s beauty survives partly because someone is always watching its frontiers. Eltnen Eltnen is Elysea’s distinctly arid region, a landscape of dry badlands, exposed stone, scarce water, and scattered greener pockets where life gathers. Its harsher terrain contrasts sharply with Poeta’s fertility and demonstrates that the southern realm is not uniformly lush. Settlements and travelers must respect distance, water, weather, and the limits imposed by the land. Ruins and isolated routes can feel especially exposed beneath the bright Elysean sky. Life in Eltnen is shaped by adaptation rather than abundance. Daevas operating here may protect water access, cross dangerous open country, investigate remote ruins, escort travelers, or respond to threats that exploit the region’s isolation. Communities that endure here have practical knowledge of the terrain and should feel capable rather than helpless. Eltnen gives Elyos adventures a frontier defined as much by environment and distance as by warfare. Heiron Heiron is a forested and mountainous region of Elysea, rich in waterways, steep terrain, old roads, and places where wilderness can conceal history. Its dense landscapes and changes in elevation distinguish it from both arid Eltnen and rural Poeta. The region carries a strong sense of vigilance and memory, with civilization existing beside terrain that can quickly become difficult or dangerous. Water, forest, and stone shape both travel and settlement. For Daevas, Heiron favors scouting, pursuit, defense, historical investigation, and expeditions into places where the landscape can hide ruins or hostile movement. Roads and communities remain important, but control of a route does not mean control of everything beyond it. The region can support stories about protecting settlements while uncovering traces of earlier ages. Heiron’s beauty is therefore inseparable from the need to remain watchful. Theobomos Theobomos is a scorched and devastated eastern island whose landscape bears wounds that ordinary weather and time have not erased. Ruins, archaeological sites, burned terrain, and supernatural scars make it one of Elysea’s clearest reminders that the wars of Atreia can permanently change the land. The region is not simply empty destruction; expeditions, researchers, soldiers, and those reclaiming knowledge still have reasons to enter it. Its damaged environment gives every surviving structure and recovered record unusual weight. Daevas come to Theobomos to investigate the past, secure dangerous sites, recover history,

desc: In the south, survivors rebuilt beneath the brighter skies of Elysea . Their people became the Asmodians, guided by the Lords later known as the Shedim Lords . These ident
text: Elysea and Asmodae In the south, survivors rebuilt beneath the brighter skies of Elysea . Over generations, their civilization became the Elyos, and the Lords who guided them came to be known as the Seraphim Lords . In the north, the survivors of Asmodae endured a harsher land. Their people became the Asmodians, guided by the Lords later known as the Shedim Lords . These identities were born after the Cataclysm. The Seraphim and Shedim were not ancient rival orders that had always existed; they emerged from survival, reconstruction, and the different beliefs that developed on each side of the broken world. Separated for generations, Elyos and Asmodians came to understand the Cataclysm—and one another—through very different histories. By the time the two peoples could meet again, neither saw the other simply as long-lost kin.

text: Entertainer What Is an Entertainer?. An Entertainer has experience performing for others as a musician, singer, dancer, actor, storyteller, comedian, public speaker, or another kind of performer. Life and Origins. Performance may have begun in taverns, public squares, a troupe, a wealthy household, a traveling company, or under a mentor. Some Entertainers knew fame; others struggled for every audience. Motivations and Outlook. Fame, recognition, wealth, inspiration, new audiences, unforgettable stories, or the desire to preserve memories can all lead an Entertainer into adventure. Playing an Entertainer. Choose what you performed and why. Your character may love attention or be quiet away from the stage. The Background does not require you, the player, to perform at the table.

title: Equipment Damage and Repair
desc: Ordinary combat does not damage gear. Equipment is damaged only by explicit effects or catastrophic circumstances. A Damaged item provides none of its normal mechanical benefits until repaired. A Destroyed item is unusable and cannot be restored by an ordinary repair. Repairing a Damaged weapon, armor, shield, or other repairable equipment uses an appropriat
text: Equipment Damage and Repair Ordinary combat does not damage gear. Equipment is damaged only by explicit effects or catastrophic circumstances. A Damaged item provides none of its normal mechanical benefits until repaired. A Destroyed item is unusable and cannot be restored by an ordinary repair. Repairing a Damaged weapon, armor, shield, or other repairable equipment uses an appropriate specialist and any GM-determined Kinah/resource cost. The player makes two separate flat d20 rolls, both DC 10, with no modifiers unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Roll 1 determines Completion Time: success = 1 hour, failure = 2 hours. After that time has elapsed, Roll 2 determines the Repair Result: success repairs the item; failure means the repair fails. Any Kinah or resources already committed are not refunded on failure. A physically repaired Aether item retains its quality and does not require paying its enhancement cost again unless the enhancement itself was specifically disrupted. Destroyed items still cannot be restored by an ordinary repair.

title: Equipment, Professions & Economy
desc: Does armor inherently give Stealth Advantage or Disadvantage? No. Armor creates no inherent Stealth Advantage or Disadvantage unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Is there a universal magic-item attunement limit? No universal attunement-slot subsystem exists. Can Professions craft complete weapons and armor from nothing? No. Weaponsmithing, Armorcrafting,
text: Equipment, Professions & Economy Does armor inherently give Stealth Advantage or Disadvantage? No. Armor creates no inherent Stealth Advantage or Disadvantage unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Is there a universal magic-item attunement limit? No universal attunement-slot subsystem exists. Can Professions craft complete weapons and armor from nothing? No. Weaponsmithing, Armorcrafting, and Handicrafting are primarily upgrade professions under the approved equipment ladder rather than a general manufacture-from-nothing system. How many Professions can be Active? One Profession is Active at a time. Changing the Active Profession occurs only on level-up. Ranks and prior progress in inactive Professions are retained.

text: Example Combat Sequence Cast a debuff through Shared Aether so the spell originates from the spirit’s position, then command the spirit to attack the same or another hostile. If both halves successfully affect hostiles during the turn, generate 1 Spirit Bond. Spend Bonded Assault only after the spirit hits, preserving Bond if the attack misses. text: Example Combat Sequences Level 5: land Sneak Attack, carve 1 Mark, immediately make Assassination Sequence; if the follow-up also hits the same target, the two-hit alternative can establish the next Mark on later levels. Shadow Step can reposition after the qualifying Sneak hit. Level 9: Sneak Attack + Sequence both hit the same target. Normal Rune Carving places 1 Mark after the Sneak hit, then Masterful Carving places another after the follow-up, preparing 2 Marks in one turn. Level 11: if that sequence brings the creature to 3 Marks, spend your Bonus Action on Execution Strike and consume the prepared pattern with a Greater Execution. Executioner: delay the three-Mark cash-out until the target is wounded, then combine Deep Carving, the expanded crit range, and Greater/Apex Execution dice. Phantom: Sneak Attack -> Shadow Step -> Hide through Vanishing Step -> become Invisible through Veiled Passage -> choose when to re-engage. Nightstalker: place a Mark to establish quarry, use Aether Trace/tracking to deny concealment, and save your Reaction for Relentless Quarry or No Escape rather than an ordinary Opportunity Attack. ← Back to Classes

text: Example Combat Sequences Level 5 baseline: move 15 feet toward a hostile, hit to generate Momentum and open the Chain, apply Driving Strike, make the second attack and apply Hamstring Strike, then continue the Chain next turn if no Finisher was affordable. Level 11 prepared Chain: Opener → Driving Strike → Hamstring Strike across the available attacks/turns → Devastating Finisher once two prior Links exist. Momentum Mastery refunds one Link expenditure along the way. Destroyer: build a full Chain and delay the Finisher until the target reaches half HP, then use the widened critical window and extra Chain Die. Tempest: position a polearm so multiple hostiles remain in reach, then use Sweeping Strike each turn to pressure clustered enemies without creating extra attack rolls. Warpath: approach through difficult terrain, trigger Battle Rush, force an Overrun save, then use Breakthrough to pass the target and threaten the formation behind it.

title: Example Combat Sequences
desc: Baseline setup: deploy a trap before the enemy reaches your lane. When it triggers, use Exploit Opening for Advantage, then spend Focus on Precision Shot or Pinning Shot only if the extra damage/control changes the turn. Level 9 sustain: move at least 15 feet from your starting position, hit with a ranged attack, then regain 1 Focus through Hunter’s Rhythm.
text: Example Combat Sequences Baseline setup: deploy a trap before the enemy reaches your lane. When it triggers, use Exploit Opening for Advantage, then spend Focus on Precision Shot or Pinning Shot only if the extra damage/control changes the turn. Level 9 sustain: move at least 15 feet from your starting position, hit with a ranged attack, then regain 1 Focus through Hunter’s Rhythm. This supports an active skirmishing loop rather than infinite Focus from standing still and firing. Level 11 trap payoff: a hostile triggers a trap and becomes Exposed. Make an Exploit Opening attack with Advantage and add 2d8 from Exploit Weakness on the hit; use Focus Mastery to reduce one technique to 0 if useful. Trapper: maintain a wider network, use Hair-Trigger when an enemy truly fails a trap save, then use Chain Reaction once on your turn to sequence a second legal trap without allowing recursion. Windrunner: move before the shot, apply Slipstream/Flowing Assault, then use the granted safe movement to preserve distance and qualify movement-based Focus recovery. ← Back to Classes

If the redirection prevents damage to the ally, Protect the Vulnerable
text: Example Defensive Sequences An enemy attacks a Challenged ally: Defy the Templar generates Resolve because you were a valid target. If you are a Justicar and the enemy remains in reach, Retributive Challenge can answer after the attack resolves. An adjacent ally is hit: Guardian’s Intercession redirects the attack. If the redirection prevents damage to the ally, Protect the Vulnerable grants Resolve before redirected damage is applied; that Resolve can immediately pay Resolute Guard. At Level 14, Guardian’s Shelter turns an ally’s save from failure to success. Protect the Vulnerable generates Resolve, then Resolute Shelter may immediately spend that Resolve to turn the successful half-damage result into no damage. A Level 17 Bulwark intercepts a lethal attack: No One Falls can supply the emergency Intercession, Last Wall spends 1 Resolve for resistance, then Resolute Guard can reduce the already-halved damage further.

text: Example Performance Sequence Cast a Harmony spell that meaningfully heals two allies: Harmonic Support may generate Resonance, then create Harmony Refrain. Next turn cast a Requiem spell: if it successfully affects a hostile and differs from your previous Song Role, Contrasting Verse may generate Resonance. The Requiem spell may create or replace a Requiem Refrain subject to your active-Refrain limit. Spend Crescendo only on the specific creature whose healing/damage needs amplification. Because Crescendo is secondary, it does not recursively trigger another Refrain or generate Resonance. At Level 15, maintain three different Refrains and use Perfect Echo Weaving to shape the new one. At Level 18, Grand Symphony expands to all four roles. At Level 20, Grand Crescendo accelerates the performance but still does not grant another full spellcasting Action or allow Refrain recursion. ← Back to Classes

text: Example Rhythm Sequence Turn A: hit with a weapon attack (Martial), then later cast a Chanter spell that meaningfully affects a creature (Spell). Because the category changed, the second qualifying event can generate Cadence under the normal once-per-turn rule or Improved Cadence at higher level. At Level 5, cast an Action Chanter spell, then use Rhythmic Strike for one Bonus Action weapon attack. This is not a second Attack action and does not grant a third standard attack. At Level 7+, change one Mantra slot to create a meaningful Chant event, apply Mantra Weaving/Harmonic Transition, and continue the Martial–Spell–Chant cycle. At high level, Network/Harmonic riders are secondary effects: they improve allies but do not recursively count as new qualifying Cadence actions unless a feature explicitly says they do. ← Back to Classes

text: Example Support Sequence An ally below half HP is healed by your Cleric spell. Healing Doctrine adds PB, the event qualifies as Meaningful Support and generates 1 Grace if your once-per-round generation is available. On a later enemy turn, that ally takes heavy attack damage. Protective Grace uses your Reaction and 1 Grace to reduce damage; if at least PB damage is actually prevented, it can generate the next available off-turn Grace event. The second Attack-action Bastion weapon attack remains a normal attack; if both hit at Level 5, Improved Core Systems reduces Heat by 1 after both resolve. If you need the other configuration, Reconfigure before or after the Attack action using your Bo
text: Example System Sequence Attack with the currently active Bastion weapon. On one hit, spend 1 Core and gain 1 Heat for Powered Shot. The second Attack-action Bastion weapon attack remains a normal attack; if both hit at Level 5, Improved Core Systems reduces Heat by 1 after both resolve. If you need the other configuration, Reconfigure before or after the Attack action using your Bonus Action; switching grants no additional attack. At Level 9, if the attack itself spent no Core and satisfies Core Cycling, regain Core after the attack under its once-per-turn limit. Do not treat a refund as a new Core-generation trigger. When Heat reaches Pressurized territory, decide whether the +2 weapon damage is worth staying hot. Vent as a Bonus Action when the risk of Overheat outweighs the extra pressure. At Level 11, Twin-System can integrate one auxiliary system into the Attack action. It still does not provide a second Attack action or a second independent Bastion turn. At Level 15, Overdrive intentionally crosses maximum Heat for one turn, then forces Overheat after end-of-turn effects; Emergency Plating cannot cancel the Overheat damage. ← Back to Classes

text: Exhaustion 6 — Collapse Procedure At Exhaustion 6 you become Unconscious and begin making Death Saving Throws; Exhaustion itself does not reduce your HP to 0. Roll 1d20 at the start of each turn with no modifiers: 10–20 is one success, 1–9 is one failure, a natural 1 is exactly one failure, and a natural 20 restores 1 HP and clears the Death Save track in the normal Dying state. text: Exploit Opening Once on each of your own turns, when you make a ranged weapon attack against a creature that triggered one of your Ranger Traps since the end of your previous turn, you may make that attack with Advantage. Specializations — Read Before You Choose Ranger chooses an initial Specialization at Level 3. Use this preview before reading the Level 1–20 progression so you can see the playstyle each path develops into. Specialization features are gained at Levels 3, 6, 10, and 14. Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Deadeye Patient precision archer Rewards controlled positioning, careful aim, cover penetration, and powerful finishing shots. Best for players who prefer measured ranged accuracy over constant movement. Trapper Trap-network controller Expands known and active traps, improves their riders, and eventually chains or remotely triggers them. Best for players who enjoy preparation, zones, and controlling where enemies can safely move. Windrunner Mobile combat archer Strengthens Quick Reposition, movement-based damage, defensive momentum, and flowing attacks. Best for players who want to stay in motion while maintaining ranged pressure. Specialization Advancement Preview Level Deadeye Trapper Windrunner 3 Patient Aim — movement-limited free damage. Expanded Trapcraft / Potent Traps — more known/active traps and failed-save rider. Mobile Archer / Running Shot — longer Quick Reposition and movement damage. 6 Steady Hand — stationary cover penetration or trapped-target 19–20 crit. Hair-Trigger — Reaction ranged attack after failed trap save. Slipstream Shot — movement-based +1d6 and safe step. 10 Kill Zone — trapped Patient Aim hit gains weapon die and can ignore resistance. Chain Reaction — one triggered trap can sequence into one different trap. Untouchable Momentum — 20-ft movement plus hit grants movement/AC/emergency Focus choice. 14 Perfect Shot — spend Focus for Piercing/Killing/Unerring shot. Master Trapper / Remote Trigger — larger network and controlled remote activation. Gale Step / Flowing Assault — safe 10-ft movement and 2d6 Slipstream after 30 ft. Specialization Reassignment Initial choice — Level 3. Choose one Specialization available to your class. Reassignment checkpoints — Levels 6, 10, and 14. When gaining one of these levels, you may either continue your current Specialization or change to another Specialization available to your class. If you change Specialization, remove every feature granted by the previous Specialization and replace it with the complete feature package of the newly selected Specialization through your current checkpoint . Features from different Specializations cannot be mixed, retained, or combined. When newly entering a Specialization, make any choices required by the features you now gain. Continuing the same Specialization does not reset earlier internal choices unless an explicit feature says otherwise. If the removed Specialization granted extra known options, selections, capacities, or Specialization-dependent maxima, remove, reselect, or recalculate them as necessary to satisfy the new path. Reassignment itself does not restore HP or class resources, and current values cannot remain above any new maximum. Reassignment occurs only as part of gaining Level 6, Level 10, or Level 14 . It cannot be performed through a rest, downtime, training, ordinary retraining, or between adventures. The Level 14 decision is the final normal Specialization choice and remains locked through Level 20 unless a later explicit rule says otherwise.

title: Exploration & Interaction
desc: Vision, stealth, traps, locks, theft, hazards, social rules, chases, and loot.
text: Player Rules Exploration & Interaction Vision, stealth, traps, locks, theft, hazards, social rules, chases, and loot. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Attitudes NPC attitudes are Friendly, Neutral, or Hostile. Roleplay comes first; a roll is used only when outcome and consequence are uncertain. Common skills include Persuasion, Deception, Intimidation, Insight, and Investigation. Plausibility A social check cannot force an impossible concession or make an NPC believe something fundamentally implausible without exceptional circumstances. Leverage affects what is possible and can influence DCs, but it does not automatically grant Advantage. Interrogation An interrogated NPC can reveal only information they actually know. Resolve one meaningful line of questioning at a time. Failure may close that approach, create resistance, or produce consequences; repeated checks need changed circumstances. Insight is not mind reading. Deception may oppose Insight when appropriate. Intimidation can succeed while still creating later consequences. Information Gathering Information comes from plausible sources. Common knowledge needs no roll. Use the skill that matches the approach. Rumors may be Reliable, Uncertain, or False, but the GM does not label them for the players. Independent sources and evidence can verify claims. Restricted information requires access. There is no fixed universal gathering-time formula and no check spam. Captivity and Restraints Physical restraints use Restrained when their actual effect warrants it. Binding an unwilling conscious creature in combat requires control first and normally an Action. Escape can use Sleight of Hand, Athletics, or Acrobatics against the restraint’s DC. A locked cell does not automatically impose Restrained. Restrained does not inherently prevent spellcasting, but implement and action requirements still matter. Ordinary restraints do not suppress Wings, Aetheric Reconstitution, or class powers unless an explicit specialized restraint says so. Transporting prisoners uses ordinary logistics. Interrogation remains a separate social procedure. Chases, Morale, Escorts & Creature Transport Chases Band Approximate Separation Engaged Immediate reach / melee contact Close 30

text: External Storage External storage is location-based and never increases personal inventory limits. Items stored externally do not count against personal slots. There is no universal external-storage slot formula; the GM judges reasonable capacity. Physical access. Stored items can be used only when physically accessible; no magical shared or remote inventory exists unless an explicit effect says so. Retrieval. Uses ordinary physical access and object-interaction timing. Ownership. Party storage is governed by player agreement, not point shares. Security. Genuinely secure player-controlled storage is normally assumed safe unless the story establishes a reason otherwise. Bulk logistics. Moving large quantities uses labor, repeated trips, faction help, and story logistics rather than weight formulas. Oversized objects. Handled narratively rather than assigned arbitrary slot counts. Temporary storage. Story-specific temporary storage is allowed. Campaign restrictions. text: Falling Onto Creatures The lower creature makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On success it avoids the collision and the falling creature takes normal fall damage. text: Final Chamber — Ultimate Ability Ultimate Activation - 100 DP. As your Action and Bonus Action, choose the option matching a Pistol or Musket you are wielding. Final Chamber requires no loaded shot, expends no ammunition, and ignores ordinary Reload and firing-cadence limits. On a hit, the attack deals its normal weapon damage plus fixed Piercing damage of 100 at Levels 10-14, 120 at Levels 15-19, or 140 at Level 20. Each makes a DEX save against DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your DEX modifier, taking fixed Piercing damage of 40 at Levels 10-14, 50 at Levels 15-19, or 60 at Level 20 on a failure, or half that amount on a success. Musket - Final Shot. Make one Ultimate Musket attack against a creature within the Musket's normal range. On a hit, the attack deals its normal weapon damage plus fixed Piercing damage of 140 at Levels 10-14, 160 at Levels 15-19, or 180 at Level 20. Final Shot ignores Half Cover; Full Cover remains absolute. It affects no secondary creatures.

title: Final Class Identity
desc: The Gunslinger is strongest when the fight never interrupts: shoot, move, reload, spend Tempo, and keep the sequence alive. Pistolero is the highest-volume Gunslinger and leads sustained direct firearm pressure. Deadeye sacrifices mobility for distance, critical pressure, and precision. Saboteur gives up direct damage for soft control and enemy-tempo disrupt
text: Final Class Identity The Gunslinger is strongest when the fight never interrupts: shoot, move, reload, spend Tempo, and keep the sequence alive. Pistolero is the highest-volume Gunslinger and leads sustained direct firearm pressure. Deadeye sacrifices mobility for distance, critical pressure, and precision. Saboteur gives up direct damage for soft control and enemy-tempo disruption. The class never gains a second Attack Action. A Pistol Gunslinger's normal high-level attack ceiling remains two Attack Action attacks plus one Quick Shot. A Musket Gunslinger instead makes the two Attack Action attacks and concentrates Tempo into Deliberate Shot rather than gaining a third attack. Class power comes from Tempo economy, reload sequencing, mobility, weapon identity, and specialization riders rather than unconditional extra attacks.

text: Player Rules Flight Exploration flight, Combat Flight Slots, airborne movement, gliding, falling, and Aether restrictions. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers 3D Distance Melee Descending Attack Physical Ranged Attacks Flight Slots Aether State Interaction Flight & Aerial Combat Altitude Layers Layer Height Ground 0 ft Low 30 ft Mid 60 ft High 90 ft Voluntarily ascending or descending one altitude layer consumes all movement for that turn. A creature cannot both ascend and descend voluntarily in the same turn. Dash does not permit an additional altitude-layer change. 3D Distance For WoA aerial targeting, total distance = the greater of horizontal distance or vertical distance. Do not use Pythagorean distance and do not add horizontal and vertical distance together. Melee Airborne melee uses ordinary reach: usually 5 feet, or 10 feet for a Reach weapon. Being on the same altitude layer does not remove the need to physically move into reach. Descending Attack If a melee attacker begins its turn higher than the target, descends at least 25 feet, and then makes its first qualifying melee attack against that lower target, the attack has Advantage. Physical Ranged Attacks A lower-altitude physical ranged attacker has Advantage against a higher-altitude winged airborne target because the wings are exposed. This Exposed Wings rule does not apply to wingless creatures flying through Saturated Aether. A higher-altitude ranged attacker gains no automatic Advantage merely for being above the target. When the physical ranged attacker is above the target, increase only the weapon’s Maximum Range by half the vertical distance, rounded up. Minimum Range is unchanged. Magical attacks do not gain this extension. Flight Slots Level Base Max Slots 1–3 2 4–6 3 7–9 4 10–12 5 13–16 6 17–19 7 20 8 A stable airborne Daeva spends 1 Flight Slot at the end of each of its turns. A grounded Daeva recovers 1 Flight Slot at the end of each grounded turn. Short Rest restores half maximum, rounded down; Long Rest restores all. When a creature runs out of Flight Slots while airborne, it immediately falls. Aether State Interaction Depleted Aether. Flight is fully restricted. Stable Aether. Normal flight rules. Saturated Aether. Daevas spend no combat Flight Slots, though exploration Flight Time limits still apply. Wingless creatures capable of movement may gain flight equal to normal Speed while Saturated; they do not use Flight Slots and are not subject to Exposed Wings. Unstable Zone / Aether Instability. This is hazard-defined scene behavior rather than a universal Aether State. The three universal States are Stable, Depleted, and Saturated. Use the specific Aether Hazard rules for the area. Aether-State Changes and Boundaries Aether-State changes take effect immediately. Crossing into a new Aether State immediately applies the entered State. In Depleted Aether, Aether-supported flight is unavailable; an airborne Daeva entering a Depleted area loses flight and falls, using the normal DC 12 Dexterity Emergency Landing Reaction if eligible. Saturated → Stable: Daevas resume normal Flight Slot expenditure. A creature flying only because Saturated Aether granted it flight loses that flight and falls. Saturated → Depleted: affected airborne creatures immediately lose Aether-supported flight and fall. Stable → Saturated: Daevas stop spending Combat Flight Slots, and eligible wingless creatures gain access to Aether-supported flight equal to normal Speed, but no creature automatically takes off. Falling and Emergency Landing Falling damage is 1d6 per 10 feet fallen, maximum 20d6. A falling creature normally lands Prone unless an explicit effect says otherwise. When Flight Slot depletion causes a fall, the creature may use its Reaction for a DC 12 Dexterity save. Success halves fall damage; failure or no Reaction takes full damage. Controlled Descent changes a successful Emergency Landing to 0 fall damage according to that feat. Falling Onto Creatures The lower creature makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On success it avoids the collision and the falling creature takes normal fall damage. On failure, roll normal fall damage once, split the total equally between the two creatures rounded down, and both become Prone. A falling creature two or more sizes smaller gives the lower creature Advantage; two or more sizes larger gives Disadvantage. This collision does not override the universal protection for creatures already Dying at 0 HP. An intentional body slam requires an improvised Action rather than granting a free collision attack. Aerial Rescue A flying rescuer with a valid path and free Reaction may attempt DC 12 Dexterity (Acrobatics) to catch a falling creature. Success stops the fall and prevents fall damage. Failure lets the fall continue. Carrying then uses the normal creature-carrying rules, prohibits voluntary ascent, and continues consuming Flight Slots. Dropped Objects An unsecured held object dropped or disarmed while airborne falls. It is not automatically damaged. Deliberately dropping an object onto a creature requires an Action, improvised attack, or hazard procedure. A creature with a free hand may use its Reaction and attempt DC 12 Acrobatics to catch an unattended falling object when physically plausible; the GM may adjust the DC. Secured inventory does not spill merely because the bearer falls. Exploration Flight Level Flight Time Flight Distance 1–2 1 min 30 ft 3–4 3 min 50 ft 5–7 4 min 70 ft 8–9 6 min 100 ft 10–12 8 min 120 ft 13–15 10 min 140 ft 16–17 12 min 160 ft 18–20 15 min 180 ft The table is titled Flight Time & Distance; older references calling the second value “speed” are obsolete. Gliding Exploration gliding requires at least 30 feet of descent, functioning open wings, and an Aether state that permits flight. It travels 3 feet horizontally per 1 foot descended, consumes neither Flight Time nor Flight Slots, always loses altitude, and has a 1-hour cooldown between glides. Master Glider improves the ratio to 4:1. ← Back to Rules

text: Flight, Critical Hits, and Range Gunslinger firearms are physical ranged weapons and use the universal altitude-based physical ranged range increase. Apply class-feature firearm range modifications first, then apply the universal altitude increase. Running Fire, Evasive Shot, Bullet Time movement, and similar effects grant ordinary movement only and do not bypass universal altitude-band change rules. Close-Quarters Gunplay functions while airborne. Firearm critical hits use the universal Wings of Atreia critical rule: double only rolled damage dice belonging to the attack; flat modifiers are not doubled. Crossfire, Grand Barrage, Lethal Calibration, Deadly Rhythm, Climactic Shot, and similar post-hit riders are not automatically doubled on a critical hit unless explicitly stated.

text: Focused Casting At Level 2 choose one Focused Casting doctrine. Focused Casting modifies a spell you shape with Aether Focus; it does not grant another spell, another Action, or a new specialization. Focused Casting Doctrine Exact Benefit Stable Channel Once on each of your turns when you apply Spell Shaping to a Sorcerer spell that deals rolled damage, you may reroll one damage die rolled for that casting that shows 1 or 2. You must use the new result. Only one die can be rerolled for that casting through this doctrine. Precise Projection Once on each of your turns when you apply Spell Shaping to a Sorcerer spell with an area of effect, choose one creature you can see in that area. That creature is unaffected by that casting. This does not change the spell’s origin, range, area size, or Full Cover restrictions. Anchored Concentration When you apply Spell Shaping to a Sorcerer spell that requires Concentration, that Concentration is Anchored. The first time before the start of your next turn that a hostile spell or feature would directly end that Concentration without making you Incapacitated, ignore that effect. Anchored Concentration cannot prevent Concentration from ending because you become Incapacitated, voluntarily end it, or begin another Concentration effect. Specializations — Read Before You Choose Sorcerer chooses an initial Specialization at Level 3. Use this preview before reading the Level 1–20 progression so you can see the playstyle each path develops into. Specialization features are gained at Levels 3, 6, 10, and 14. Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Elementalist Devoted elemental specialist Commits to Fire, Ice, or Lightning and progressively strengthens that element’s damage or control rider. Best for players who want a strong elemental identity and straightforward spell pressure. Spellbinder Arcane control specialist Adds seals, area manipulation, Concentration protection, and increasingly firm constraints on enemy movement and reactions. Best for players who enjoy battlefield control and spell geometry. Aether Sage Aether Focus and shaping specialist Expands Focus capacity, casting doctrines, shaping flexibility, and resource efficiency. Best for players who want the most adaptable version of the Sorcerer’s core spell-shaping engine. Specialization Advancement Preview Level Elementalist Spellbinder Aether Sage 3 Elemental Devotion — Fire damage, Ice slow, or Lightning attack penalty. Arcane Seal — failed save creates Anchor or Disrupt. Deep Reservoir — +1 max Focus and +1 Short Rest recovery. 6 Focused Element — shaped devoted spells gain elemental rider. Binding Geometry + Anchored Formula — move persistent areas and protect against the specific failed saving throws that would directly end an existing Concentration effect. Adaptive Doctrine — two Focused Casting choices. 10 Elemental Mastery — +INT damage and resistance bypass once/turn. Residual Constraint — successful saves still suffer a small soft-control residue. Efficient Channel — rest-based discount plus bounded refund. 14 Elemental Ascendance — strongest devoted-element rider. Perfect Binding — bounded Speed/Reaction or Dash/attack control. Triune Shaping — all three shaping modes, improved reservoir and all doctrines. Specialization Reassignment Initial choice — Level 3. Choose one Specialization available to your class. Reassignment checkpoints — Levels 6, 10, and 14. When gaining one of these levels, you may either continue your current Specialization or change to another Specialization available to your class. If you change Specialization, remove every feature granted by the previous Specialization and replace it with the complete feature package of the newly selected Specialization through your current checkpoint . Features from different Specializations cannot be mixed, retained, or combined. When newly entering a Specialization, make any choices required by the features you now gain. Continuing the same Specialization does not reset earlier internal choices unless an explicit feature says otherwise. If the removed Specialization granted extra known options, selections, capacities, or Specialization-dependent maxima, remove, reselect, or recalculate them as necessary to satisfy the new path. Reassignment itself does not restore HP or class resources, and current values cannot remain above any new maximum. Reassignment occurs only as part of gaining Level 6, Level 10, or Level 14 . It cannot be performed through a rest, downtime, training, ordinary retraining, or between adventures. The Level 14 decision is the final normal Specialization choice and remains locked through Level 20 unless a later explicit rule says otherwise.
