text: Fortress Wars Player Rules Legions & Complete Abyss Warfront System Player-created Legions plus the complete player-operable Warfront rules, unit catalogue, War Asset costs, Fortress procedures, and Open Abyss procedures. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Core Rulebook v4.2 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026 , synchronized with Player Handbook v3.10 . This page exposes the complete player-operable Warfront subsystem. Explicitly GM-facing enemy statblocks, hidden force composition, and closed GM-only resolution tables remain off the public player site. Legions Warfront Overview War Assets Unit Statistics Battle Exchange Unit Catalogue Unit Costs PC Participation Fortress Wars Open Abyss Reinforcements Quick Reference PLAYER-CREATED LEGIONS A player-created Legion is a lightweight organization for shared identity, missions, resources, and cross-faction cooperation when the campaign permits it. Legion membership does not create a new character progression track or grant automatic combat bonuses. When a Legion Can Be Founded Campaign Gate. The Campaign Director or controlling GM must explicitly declare Legion Founding available. Reaching Level 11 by itself does not unlock the system. Founding Player. One Founding Player must be Level 11 or higher. That character becomes the initial Legion Leader. Other members. Every other founding or joining member must be Level 3 or higher before joining and must already have reached their Specialization or Archetype choice where applicable. A Level 1-2 character cannot join early. Membership has no maximum size. There is no minimum number of additional founders; a qualifying Founding Player may establish the Legion alone if all other founding requirements are satisfied. Elyos and Asmodians may belong to the same Legion once the required campaign state is active. Every member retains their original faction identity and its normal consequences. Founding Fund and Treasury Founding requires 5,000 Kinah deposited into the new Legion Treasury. Eligible founding members may contribute toward the total. Before establishment, the Founding Fund cannot be withdrawn. If founding is abandoned, each contributor receives their contribution back. Once established, the 5,000 Kinah remains usable Treasury money. Any Legion member may deposit Kinah. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw Kinah or authorize spending. Legion missions may reward participating members, the Treasury, or both as determined by the GM. There is no passive Legion income, automatic salary, interest, business-profit engine, or mandatory recurring membership dues. Leadership and Membership The only default roles are Legion Leader and Legion Member. The Legion Leader admits and removes members, controls permissions for Legion assets, may transfer leadership, and may formally dissolve the Legion. Leadership may be transferred to any existing legal Legion member. The new Leader does not need to be Level 11; Level 11 is a founding requirement only. Member Benefits Members may display the Legion name, colors, crest, and insignia. Ordinary Legion identification occupies no Inventory Slot. Members may accept Legion missions and may use resources, facilities, contacts, and support the Legion actually possesses when the Legion Leader permits it. Where the campaign's cross-faction arrangements recognize the Legion, its insignia provides a legitimate reason for Elyos and Asmodian members to operate together. It does not grant diplomatic immunity or unrestricted access. Legion membership grants no automatic Hit, AC, damage, HP, saving throw, skill, Advantage, Spell DC, DP, class-resource, equipment-quality, or personal Inventory bonus. Legion Storage and Headquarters An established Legion has one secure shared Storage location with a capacity of 100 Inventory Slots. Normal Inventory Slot and stacking rules apply; Kinah remains in the Treasury and uses no Storage Slots. Any Legion member may deposit eligible items. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw items or authorize another member to retrieve them. Legion Storage is stationary and cannot be accessed remotely. It never increases a member's personal Inventory capacity in the field. A Legion may designate one legitimate location as its Headquarters. The Headquarters is simply its meeting place and Storage location; it grants no automatic bonuses and has no upgrade track. Lightweight Rule. There is no Legion XP, Legion Level, officer hierarchy, skill tree, research tree, reputation meter, headquarters progression, or other default Legion management subsystem. Abyss Warfront System Warfronts resolve formation-scale warfare separately from ordinary character-scale combat. They are used for Fortress Wars and Open Abyss Battles. Strategic travel and marching between major engagements are handled narratively, off-table, or during downtime. Shared Warfront Command The player side uses one shared strategic board. Players collectively decide how to delegate Battlefronts or grids and who rolls the relevant Warfront dice. A player's PC location and that player's responsibility for rolling a different Battlefront are separate. Universal Synchronized Warfront Cycle Simultaneous Movement Phase. Both sides complete legal strategic movement in the same Movement Phase. Where opposing adjacent forces could advance directly into one another, the player side has advance-declaration priority. Battle Phase. Identify every engagement created by that movement. Every active engagement resolves completely, including all Battle Exchanges and Decision Windows. No Early New Movement. A Battlefront or grid that resolves early cannot begin a new normal strategic move while another engagement from that Battle Phase is unresolved. End-of-Battle-Phase Resolution. After all engagements conclude, resolve applicable control changes, recovery for eligible withdrawn Units, eliminations, retreats, and any External Reinforcement Check that is due. Then begin the next Movement Phase. No Zone of Control. Enemy adjacency by itself never locks movement. An engagement begins only when opposing forces legally enter or share the same Battlefront or grid. War Assets (WA) War Assets represent personnel, equipment, authorization, logistics, transportation, Aether resources, supplies, and the sustained resources needed to field formations. The GM declares a separate Base WA allowance for each participating side before force selection and deployment. The GM may restrict available Unit Catalogue options, Tiers, or Specialist formations for a specific operation. There is no recurring Warfront Upkeep. Unused operation-specific Base or Supplemental WA is not banked, transferred, or refunded. Only the player-controlled side may buy Supplemental WA with Kinah. Recommended Baseline WA Warfront Attacker Defender Open Abyss Battle 100 WA 100 WA Standard Fortress War 150 WA 100 WA Major Fortress War 350 WA 200 WA These are recommended operational baselines, not mandatory encounter budgets. text: Gelkmaros Gelkmaros is the principal Asmodian foothold on the known Balaurean frontier, a dangerous outer-world region of wilderness, Balaur infrastructure, refugee communities, fortress corridors, and routes toward Silentera. Gelkmaros Fortress anchors Asmodian operations, while places such as Rhonnam Refugee Village, Vorgaltem Citadel, Crimson Temple, and other outposts reveal a frontier shared with communities that are not simply extensions of Asmodae. Old Balaur routes and structures remain embedded in the landscape. Control is practical and local rather than absolute. Archons and other Daevas may defend refugees, negotiate with local peoples, secure routes, investigate hostile infrastructure, or undertake expeditions beyond reliable maps. The region rewards field competence and the ability to protect without assuming that protection grants ownership or assimilation. Not every Shulack or other Balaurean people encountered here is automatically hostile, making judgment as important as combat readiness. Gelkmaros is where Asmodian resilience meets a world whose conflicts are older and more complicated than the familiar rivalry with Elysea.

title: Gladiator
desc: Complete player reference for the Gladiator class in Wings of Atreia, based on Player Handbook v3.10.
text: Martial Striker • Chain Attacks • Momentum • Frontline Pressure Gladiator “Nothing can stand in my way!” The premier sustained melee damage class, built around deliberate attack sequences, Momentum, Chain Links, and Finishers. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. Overview Class Chassis Momentum Chain Attacks Action Reference Specializations Preview Levels 1–20 Combat Examples Specialization Reassignment Class Overview The Gladiator is the premier sustained melee damage class. It wins through sequences rather than single isolated attacks: open a Chain, spend Momentum on Links that alter the battlefield, then cash the sequence out with a Finisher. Polearms provide the highest sustained weapon output, while weapon discipline and specialization determine whether the Gladiator emphasizes execution, cleaving pressure, or relentless pursuit. Class Identity Gladiators are Daevas who turn martial mastery into relentless battlefield pressure. They are not defined by a single weapon or one decisive blow, but by the ability to seize momentum, force an opening, and keep an enemy under pressure until the fight breaks in their favor. In Wings of Atreia, this identity is expressed through Momentum and Chain Attacks: the Gladiator becomes more dangerous when attacks, movement, and finishers are linked into a deliberate sequence. Tradition & Outlook The Gladiator tradition descends from the broad warrior disciplines of Atreia and is associated with soldiers, arena fighters, legion veterans, weapon masters, and Daevas who believe that skill must survive contact with a real battlefield. Gladiators commonly value courage, physical discipline, adaptability, and decisive action. Some fight for glory or personal mastery; others see themselves as the hard edge of a legion, the Daeva who advances when everyone else needs the line to move. Appearance & Adventuring Gladiators usually present themselves as practical combatants: heavy armor, battle-worn weapons, and equipment chosen for reach, leverage, or sustained close combat. Polearms and other approved Gladiator weapons may suggest very different fighting schools, but the class is recognized by an aggressive, forward-driving presence. A Gladiator adventures to test mastery, protect comrades through offensive pressure, earn renown, serve a military cause, or become strong enough to face the threats of the Abyss and Balaurea directly. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Strength Secondary Ability Dexterity Hit Die d12 Saving Throws Strength, Constitution Armor Chain Armor, Plate Armor Weapons Shortswords, Longswords, Polearms, Spears Skills Choose 2: Acrobatics, Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Survival Class Save DC 8 + PB + STR modifier Signature Resource Momentum Signature Mechanic Chain Attacks Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Momentum and Chains Momentum represents the Gladiator forcing the battle forward. It exists only in genuine combat and resets to 0 when combat ends. Normal Momentum does not decay simply because you failed to spend it; later features care about maintaining an active Chain instead. First melee hit on your own turn: gain 1 Momentum. Aggressive Momentum: once on each of your turns, gain 1 additional Momentum if a melee hit follows at least 15 feet of movement toward that target, is a critical hit, or reduces a hostile creature to 0 HP. Multiple qualifying conditions on one attack still grant only 1 additional Momentum. Maximum Momentum: 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. A single attack cannot normally grant more than the Momentum allowed by the generation rules above. Refunds occur after the triggering feature resolves and are not new Momentum-generation events unless stated otherwise. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Momentum exists only in genuine combat and normally begins at 0. A later feature may cause you to begin genuine combat with Momentum instead. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. How You Gain It Your first melee hit on your own turn grants 1 Momentum. Once on each of your turns, Aggressive Momentum grants 1 additional Momentum when a melee hit follows at least 15 ft of movement toward that target, is a critical hit, or reduces a hostile creature to 0 HP. Generation Limits Multiple Aggressive Momentum conditions on one hit still grant only 1 additional Momentum. A normal hit cannot repeatedly generate Momentum beyond the explicit first-hit and Aggressive Momentum triggers. How You Spend It Driving Strike 1; Sweeping Strike 1; Crushing Finisher 2; Hamstring Strike 1; Staggering Strike 1; Devastating Finisher 3; Titanic Finisher 4; Endless Assault 1 at Levels 15–19 (0 at Level 20). Refunds / Recovery Later features may refund or grant Momentum after a Link or Finisher resolves or at a stated timing. A refund is not a new Momentum-generation event unless the feature explicitly says otherwise. Persistence / Reset Normal Momentum does not decay during combat merely because you did not spend it. It resets to 0 when combat ends. Does Not Generate Artificial combat, staged attacks, harmless allied targets, or forced movement used to imitate Battle Rush do not generate Momentum unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Chain Attacks A Chain begins when you declare a successful melee hit on your own turn to be an Opener . You can maintain only one Chain at a time. The Chain belongs to you, not to a particular enemy, so later Links may strike another legal target. A miss does not automatically end the Chain. It lasts until the end of your next turn, until you use a Finisher, abandon it, or become unable to continue it. One Chain technique may modify a given attack. Chain Links and Finishers normally apply only to attacks made on your own turn. A Finisher ends the Chain after it resolves. Chain Dice are d6 at Levels 1–4, d8 at 5–10, d10 at 11–16, and d12 at 17–20. Chain Dice added directly to the triggering weapon attack double on a critical hit. Independent secondary damage does not. Universal Gladiator Chain Techniques Technique Cost Requirement Exact Effect Driving Strike 1 Momentum A melee hit that can carry a Link Add 1 Chain Die to the attack. If the target is no more than one size larger, push it 5 feet. Sweeping Strike 1 Momentum A melee hit; once per turn Choose another hostile within your reach and within 5 feet of the original target. It takes 1 Chain Die + STR modifier damage. This is independent secondary damage, not a separate attack. Crushing Finisher 2 Momentum At least 1 prior Link Add 2 Chain Dice to the triggering attack. The Chain ends after resolution. Hamstring Strike 1 Momentum Level 5; a Link Add 1 Chain Die and reduce the target’s Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. Specializations — Read Before You Choose Cleric chooses an initial Specialization at Level 3. Use this preview before reading the Level 1–20 progression so you can see the playstyle each path develops into. Specialization features are gained at Levels 3, 6, 10, and 14. Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Healer Restoration specialist Strengthens direct healing, overflow restoration, emergency recovery, and life-saving output. Best for players who want healing to be the Cleric’s clearest primary identity. Protector Mitigation and interception specialist Turns divine protection toward guarding allies, intercepting danger, anchoring a position, and preventing damage. Best for players who prefer prevention and protection over pure recovery. Purifier Cleansing and anti-affliction specialist Improves purification, diagnosis, removal of hostile effects, and defensive cleansing. Best for players who want to counter conditions, corruption, and debilitating enemy effects. Specialization Advancement Preview Level Healer Protector Purifier 3 Overflowing Restoration; Mercy Overflow Sacred Intercession; Stand Beside Me Purifying Grace; Purifying Insight 6 Deep Restoration Consecrated Guard; Intercepting Grace Greater Purification; Aetheric Diagnosis 10 Life Overflow; Restorative Conversion Sacred Bulwark; Anchoring Presence Purging Light; Greater Diagnosis 14 Miracle of Life Unyielding Sanctuary Absolute Purification; Purifying Aegis Specialization Reassignment Initial choice — Level 3. Choose one Specialization available to your class. Reassignment checkpoints — Levels 6, 10, and 14. When gaining one of these levels, you may either continue your current Specialization or change to another Specialization available to your class. If you change Specialization, remove every feature granted by the previous Specialization and replace it with the complete feature package of the newly selected Specialization through your current checkpoint . Features from different Specializations cannot be mixed, retained, or combined. When newly entering a Specialization, make any choices required by the features you now gain. Continuing the same Specialization does not reset earlier internal choices unless an explicit feature says otherwise. If the removed Specialization granted extra known options, selections, capacities, or Specialization-dependent maxima, remove, reselect, or recalculate them as necessary to satisfy the new path. Reassignment itself does not restore HP or class resources, and current values cannot remain above any new maximum. Reassignment occurs only as part of gaining Level 6, Level 10, or Level 14 . It cannot be performed through a rest, downtime, training, ordinary retraining, or between adventures. The Level 14 decision is the final normal Specialization choice and remains locked through Level 20 unless a later explicit rule says otherwise.

title: Gunslinger
desc: Complete player reference for the Gunslinger class in Wings of Atreia, based on Player Handbook v3.10.
text: Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Role Ranged weapon damage Secondary Role Mobility, precision, disruption Primary Ability DEX Secondary Ability INT Hit Die d8 Saving Throws DEX, INT Armor Leather Weapons Pistols, Muskets Signature Resource Tempo Signature Mechanic Firearm sequencing and reload rhythm Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. Tactical Shot: when a Gunslinger class feature tied to a firearm attack meaningfully forces movement, applies a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 feet of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. A single attack can never generate more than 1 normal Tempo even if it satisfies multiple conditions. Levels 1-4: normal own-turn Tempo generation is capped at 1. From Level 5: up to 2 Tempo on your own turn, but from distinct qualifying events. From Level 17: a third Tempo on your turn is possible only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Tempo never falls below 0. If you end your turn without making a Gunslinger firearm attack or successfully using a Gunslinger firearm technique, lose 1 Tempo. At Level 13 this rule improves through Sustained Tempo. Tempo Refunds A Tempo refund is not Tempo generation unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Refunds therefore do not trigger effects that require gaining Tempo. When gaining one of these levels, you may either continue your current Specialization or change to another Specialization available to your class. If you change Specialization, remove every feature granted by the previous Specialization and replace it with the complete feature package of the newly selected Specialization through your current checkpoint . Features from different Specializations cannot be mixed, retained, or combined. When newly entering a Specialization, make any choices required by the features you now gain. text: Heat Heat returns to 0 after 1 minute outside genuine combat without intensive Bastion operation and is produced only by systems or features that explicitly say they gain Heat. text: Heiron Heiron is a forested and mountainous region of Elysea, rich in waterways, steep terrain, old roads, and places where wilderness can conceal history. Its dense landscapes and changes in elevation distinguish it from both arid Eltnen and rural Poeta. The region carries a strong sense of vigilance and memory, with civilization existing beside terrain that can quickly become difficult or dangerous. Water, forest, and stone shape both travel and settlement. For Daevas, Heiron favors scouting, pursuit, defense, historical investigation, and expeditions into places where the landscape can hide ruins or hostile movement. Roads and communities remain important, but control of a route does not mean control of everything beyond it. The region can support stories about protecting settlements while uncovering traces of earlier ages. Heiron’s beauty is therefore inseparable from the need to remain watchful.

text: Hit Dice and HP A character has Hit Dice equal to character level. text: Iluma Iluma is a recognized region of Elysea associated with sacred archaeology and the recovery of ancient memory. It belongs to the wider WoA Gazetteer even though it is outside the first-wave continental atlas, so its exact map presentation is intentionally deferred. The region is best understood as a place where the remains of earlier Atreia carry religious, historical, and cultural importance. Its identity should come from discovery and reverence rather than from importing later events as predetermined canon. For player characters, Iluma offers expeditions centered on ancient sites, contested interpretations of history, relics, and questions about what the people of the present choose to preserve. Scholars, religious authorities, soldiers, and explorers may all value the same discovery for very different reasons. The region is well suited to stories where knowledge itself has political or spiritual consequences. Because its future is not locked to later source continuity, discoveries in Iluma can belong to the campaign the players actually create.

text: Inggison Inggison is the principal Elyos foothold on the known Balaurean frontier, reached through stable physical routes that can support real military logistics. It combines dangerous wilderness, ancient Balaur infrastructure, fortress corridors, expeditionary positions, and contact with peoples who have lived under Balaur pressure far longer than most Elyos newcomers. The region is a foothold, not a conquered province, and maintained routes become less certain as expeditions move beyond established corridors. Its approaches also form one side of the strategic access toward Silentera. Daevas in Inggison may defend fortresses, escort expeditions, work with Reians and other local peoples, explore ruins, or respond to Balaur activity in territory no faction fully controls. Success often depends on coalition-building and learning from residents rather than assuming Elyos institutions already understand the outer world. The frontier can support military missions and cultural encounters in the same journey. Inggison marks the point where the familiar war of Elysea opens into the much larger uncertainty of Balaurea.

text: Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally.

text: Ishalgen Ishalgen is a rugged island frontier whose terrain and isolated communities foster a strong sense of independence. Uneven ground, wilderness, exposed routes, and local settlements make the region feel removed from the monumental scale of Pandaemonium. Its people are accustomed to solving practical problems with limited support and to respecting dangers beyond settled ground. The landscape reflects the northern world without reducing it to a frozen wasteland. Daevas in Ishalgen may be asked to protect communities, cross difficult terrain, investigate remote disturbances, or deal with threats that cannot wait for distant authorities. Local knowledge and self-reliance matter here, making cooperation with residents as important as raw power. The region is well suited to grounded adventures where a small settlement can matter as much as a fortress objective. Ishalgen expresses Asmodian resilience through independence rather than through grand military spectacle.

title: Legions & Complete Abyss Warfront System
desc: Player-created Legions and player-facing Abyss Warfront procedures.
text: Player Rules Legions & Complete Abyss Warfront System Player-created Legions plus the complete player-operable Warfront rules, unit catalogue, War Asset costs, Fortress procedures, and Open Abyss procedures. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Core Rulebook v4.2 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026 , synchronized with Player Handbook v3.10 . This page exposes the complete player-operable Warfront subsystem. Explicitly GM-facing enemy statblocks, hidden force composition, and closed GM-only resolution tables remain off the public player site. Legions Warfront Overview War Assets Unit Statistics Battle Exchange Unit Catalogue Unit Costs PC Participation Fortress Wars Open Abyss Reinforcements Quick Reference PLAYER-CREATED LEGIONS A player-created Legion is a lightweight organization for shared identity, missions, resources, and cross-faction cooperation when the campaign permits it. Legion membership does not create a new character progression track or grant automatic combat bonuses. When a Legion Can Be Founded Campaign Gate. The Campaign Director or controlling GM must explicitly declare Legion Founding available. Reaching Level 11 by itself does not unlock the system. Founding Player. One Founding Player must be Level 11 or higher. That character becomes the initial Legion Leader. Other members. Every other founding or joining member must be Level 3 or higher before joining and must already have reached their Specialization or Archetype choice where applicable. A Level 1-2 character cannot join early. Membership has no maximum size. There is no minimum number of additional founders; a qualifying Founding Player may establish the Legion alone if all other founding requirements are satisfied. Elyos and Asmodians may belong to the same Legion once the required campaign state is active. Every member retains their original faction identity and its normal consequences. Founding Fund and Treasury Founding requires 5,000 Kinah deposited into the new Legion Treasury. Eligible founding members may contribute toward the total. Before establishment, the Founding Fund cannot be withdrawn. If founding is abandoned, each contributor receives their contribution back. Once established, the 5,000 Kinah remains usable Treasury money. Any Legion member may deposit Kinah. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw Kinah or authorize spending. Legion missions may reward participating members, the Treasury, or both as determined by the GM. There is no passive Legion income, automatic salary, interest, business-profit engine, or mandatory recurring membership dues. Leadership and Membership The only default roles are Legion Leader and Legion Member. The Legion Leader admits and removes members, controls permissions for Legion assets, may transfer leadership, and may formally dissolve the Legion. Leadership may be transferred to any existing legal Legion member. The new Leader does not need to be Level 11; Level 11 is a founding requirement only. Member Benefits Members may display the Legion name, colors, crest, and insignia. Ordinary Legion identification occupies no Inventory Slot. Members may accept Legion missions and may use resources, facilities, contacts, and support the Legion actually possesses when the Legion Leader permits it. Where the campaign's cross-faction arrangements recognize the Legion, its insignia provides a legitimate reason for Elyos and Asmodian members to operate together. It does not grant diplomatic immunity or unrestricted access. Legion membership grants no automatic Hit, AC, damage, HP, saving throw, skill, Advantage, Spell DC, DP, class-resource, equipment-quality, or personal Inventory bonus. Legion Storage and Headquarters An established Legion has one secure shared Storage location with a capacity of 100 Inventory Slots. Normal Inventory Slot and stacking rules apply; Kinah remains in the Treasury and uses no Storage Slots. Any Legion member may deposit eligible items. Only the Legion Leader may withdraw items or authorize another member to retrieve them. Legion Storage is stationary and cannot be accessed remotely. It never increases a member's personal Inventory capacity in the field. A Legion may designate one legitimate location as its Headquarters. The Headquarters is simply its meeting place and Storage location; it grants no automatic bonuses and has no upgrade track. Lightweight Rule. There is no Legion XP, Legion Level, officer hierarchy, skill tree, research tree, reputation meter, headquarters progression, or other default Legion management subsystem. Abyss Warfront System Warfronts resolve formation-scale warfare separately from ordinary character-scale combat. They are used for Fortress Wars and Open Abyss Battles. Strategic travel and marching between major engagements are handled narratively, off-table, or during downtime. Shared Warfront Command The player side uses one shared strategic board. Players collectively decide how to delegate Battlefronts or grids and who rolls the relevant Warfront dice. A player's PC location and that player's responsibility for rolling a different Battlefront are separate. Universal Synchronized Warfront Cycle Simultaneous Movement Phase. Both sides complete legal strategic movement in the same Movement Phase. Where opposing adjacent forces could advance directly into one another, the player side has advance-declaration priority. Battle Phase. Identify every engagement created by that movement. Every active engagement resolves completely, including all Battle Exchanges and Decision Windows. No Early New Movement. A Battlefront or grid that resolves early cannot begin a new normal strategic move while another engagement from that Battle Phase is unresolved. End-of-Battle-Phase Resolution. After all engagements conclude, resolve applicable control changes, recovery for eligible withdrawn Units, eliminations, retreats, and any External Reinforcement Check that is due. Then begin the next Movement Phase. No Zone of Control. Enemy adjacency by itself never locks movement. An engagement begins only when opposing forces legally enter or share the same Battlefront or grid. War Assets (WA) War Assets represent personnel, equipment, authorization, logistics, transportation, Aether resources, supplies, and the sustained resources needed to field formations. The GM declares a separate Base WA allowance for each participating side before force selection and deployment. The GM may restrict available Unit Catalogue options, Tiers, or Specialist formations for a specific operation. There is no recurring Warfront Upkeep. Unused operation-specific Base or Supplemental WA is not banked, transferred, or refunded. Only the player-controlled side may buy Supplemental WA with Kinah. Recommended Baseline WA Warfront Attacker Defender Open Abyss Battle 100 WA 100 WA Standard Fortress War 150 WA 100 WA Major Fortress War 350 WA 200 WA These are recommended operational baselines, not mandatory encounter budgets. text: Legions & Warfronts Do I use my ordinary AC, damage dice, spells, and class resources directly as Warfront stats? No. Warfront scale is intentionally separate. Use the Warfront rules unless an effect explicitly says it transfers across scales. What are a PC's Warfront values? A participating PC uses ATK 3 while attacking and DEF 3 while defending . PCs are not Units, have no Tier or END, and cost no WA. Can I gain or spend DP or use my Ultimate during a Warfront? No. DP and Ultimates are inaccessible for the entire Warfront operation, including embedded character-scale missions. Existing DP is retained until the operation ends. Can PCs capture Warfront objectives by themselves? No. Objective and grid control follows the Unit rules. PCs do not independently capture Warfront objectives. When are player-created Legions available? Player-created Legions are campaign-gated organizational content. At least one founder must meet the required Level threshold, and the GM must confirm that the campaign has reached the required public state. Reaching the Level threshold by itself does not unlock or reveal hidden campaign information.

Specializations — Read Before You Choose Aethertech chooses an initial Specialization at Level 3. Use this preview before reading the Level 1–20 progression so you can see the playstyle each path develops into. Specialization features are gained at Levels 3, 6, 10, and 14. Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Siege Engineer Heavy-cannon artillery specialist Builds Aether Core and manages Heat to deliver the class’s strongest cannon bursts and siege pressure. Best for players who want deliberate setup followed by powerful ranged payoff. Bulwark Pilot Defensive Bastion specialist Strengthens Bastion durability, mitigation, interception, and protective positioning. Best for players who want to keep the combat platform standing and shield allies from pressure. Flux Engineer Core-and-Heat systems specialist Manipulates Aether Core and Heat more flexibly, converting resources and exploiting Pressurized states while controlling Overheat. Best for players who enjoy resource management and adaptable system play. Specialization Advancement Preview Level Siege Engineer Bulwark Pilot Flux Engineer 3 Heavy Cannon / Siege Calibration Fortress Plating / Intercepting Frame Heat Conversion / Flux Discharge 6 Bombardment Round / Anchored Firing Reactive Armor / Mobile Cover Thermal Cascade / Efficient Conversion 10 Penetrating Cannon / Siege Overload Defensive Core / Guardian Thrusters Thermal Reversal / Flux Lock 14 Devastation Cannon / Siege Momentum Bastion Fortress / Protective Field Reactor Feedback / Perfect Conversion Specialization Reassignment Initial choice — Level 3. Choose one Specialization available to your class. Reassignment checkpoints — Levels 6, 10, and 14. When gaining one of these levels, you may either continue your current Specialization or change to another Specialization available to your class. If you change Specialization, remove every feature granted by the previous Specialization and replace it with the complete feature package of the newly selected Specialization through your current checkpoint . Features from different Specializations cannot be mixed, retained, or combined. When newly entering a Specialization, make any choices required by the features you now gain. Continuing the same Specialization does not reset earlier internal choices unless an explicit feature says otherwise. If the removed Specialization granted extra known options, selections, capacities, or Specialization-dependent maxima, remove, reselect, or recalculate them as necessary to satisfy the new path. Reassignment itself does not restore HP or class resources, and current values cannot remain above any new maximum. Reassignment occurs only as part of gaining Level 6, Level 10, or Level 14 . It cannot be performed through a rest, downtime, training, ordinary retraining, or between adventures. The Level 14 decision is the final normal Specialization choice and remains locked through Level 20 unless a later explicit rule says otherwise.

text: Level 1 — Focus, Trapcraft and Exploit Opening Ranged Striker • Focus • Traps • Tactical Repositioning Ranger “Chase me or run away. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. Tactical Shot: when a Gunslinger class feature tied to a firearm attack meaningfully forces movement, applies a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 feet of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. A single attack can never generate more than 1 normal Tempo even if it satisfies multiple conditions. Levels 1-4: normal own-turn Tempo generation is capped at 1. From Level 5: up to 2 Tempo on your own turn, but from distinct qualifying events. From Level 17: a third Tempo on your turn is possible only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Tempo never falls below 0. If you end your turn without making a Gunslinger firearm attack or successfully using a Gunslinger firearm technique, lose 1 Tempo. At Level 13 this rule improves through Sustained Tempo. Tempo Refunds A Tempo refund is not Tempo generation unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Refunds therefore do not trigger effects that require gaining Tempo. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Tempo begins at 0 in genuine combat and resets to 0 when combat ends. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. Generation Limits A single attack creates at most 1 normal Tempo. text: Level 1 — Sneak Attack, Rune Carving, Rune Burst, Shadow Step Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. Rune Carving: once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Rune Mark after that hit resolves. Alternatively, hitting the same creature with two different melee attacks during your turn can place 1 Rune Mark after the second hit. Normal attack-based Rune placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. Newly created Rune Marks cannot be consumed by the same hit that created them. If you exceed your current marked-target limit, choose one previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Marks disappear when consumed, when the marked creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. A creature carries your Marks until they are consumed or removed. Maximum Up to 3 Rune Marks per creature. Marked-target capacity is 1 creature through Level 8, 2 from Levels 9–16, and 3 from Level 17 onward. How You Place Marks Once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Mark after the hit resolves. Alternatively, two different melee hits against the same creature during your turn can place 1 Mark after the second hit. Placement Limits Normal attack-based placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless an explicit feature increases it. A newly created Mark cannot be consumed by the hit that created it. How You Spend Them On a hit against a marked creature, Rune Burst and later Execution features consume the stated number of Marks to add Rune Dice or execution riders. Changing Targets If you exceed your marked-target capacity, choose a previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Removal / Reset Marks disappear when consumed, when the creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered. text: Level 11 — Greater Rune Execution and Execution Strike Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. Rune Carving: once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Rune Mark after that hit resolves. Alternatively, hitting the same creature with two different melee attacks during your turn can place 1 Rune Mark after the second hit. Normal attack-based Rune placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. Newly created Rune Marks cannot be consumed by the same hit that created them. If you exceed your current marked-target limit, choose one previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Marks disappear when consumed, when the marked creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Resource Form Rune Marks are target-bound counters, not a generic personal pool. A creature carries your Marks until they are consumed or removed. Maximum Up to 3 Rune Marks per creature. Marked-target capacity is 1 creature through Level 8, 2 from Levels 9–16, and 3 from Level 17 onward. How You Place Marks Once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Mark after the hit resolves. Alternatively, two different melee hits against the same creature during your turn can place 1 Mark after the second hit. Placement Limits Normal attack-based placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless an explicit feature increases it. A newly created Mark cannot be consumed by the hit that created it. How You Spend Them On a hit against a marked creature, Rune Burst and later Execution features consume the stated number of Marks to add Rune Dice or execution riders. Changing Targets If you exceed your marked-target capacity, choose a previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Removal / Reset Marks disappear when consumed, when the creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. Does Not Generate Missing, merely targeting, off-turn staged attacks, or hitting a creature without satisfying Rune Carving do not place Marks unless an explicit Assassin feature says otherwise. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Role Ranged weapon damage Secondary Role Mobility, precision, disruption Primary Ability DEX Secondary Ability INT Hit Die d8 Saving Throws DEX, INT Armor Leather Weapons Pistols, Muskets Signature Resource Tempo Signature Mechanic Firearm sequencing and reload rhythm Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. Tactical Shot: when a Gunslinger class feature tied to a firearm attack meaningfully forces movement, applies a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 feet of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. A single attack can never generate more than 1 normal Tempo even if it satisfies multiple conditions. Levels 1-4: normal own-turn Tempo generation is capped at 1. From Level 5: up to 2 Tempo on your own turn, but from distinct qualifying events. From Level 17: a third Tempo on your turn is possible only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Tempo never falls below 0. If you end your turn without making a Gunslinger firearm attack or successfully using a Gunslinger firearm technique, lose 1 Tempo. At Level 13 this rule improves through Sustained Tempo. Tempo Refunds A Tempo refund is not Tempo generation unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Refunds therefore do not trigger effects that require gaining Tempo. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Tempo begins at 0 in genuine combat and resets to 0 when combat ends. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. How You Gain It — Clean Hit After you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits. How You Gain It — Tactical Shot When a Gunslinger firearm technique meaningfully forces movement, imposes a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 ft of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits. Generation Limits A single attack creates at most 1 normal Tempo. Own-turn generation cap: 1 at Levels 1–4; up to 2 from Level 5 using distinct qualifying events; a third at Level 17+ only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. Rune Carving: once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Rune Mark after that hit resolves. Alternatively, hitting the same creature with two different melee attacks during your turn can place 1 Rune Mark after the second hit. Normal attack-based Rune placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. Newly created Rune Marks cannot be consumed by the same hit that created them. If you exceed your current marked-target limit, choose one previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Marks disappear when consumed, when the marked creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d10 Saving Throws Dexterity, Strength Armor Leather Armor Weapons Longbows, Shortbows, Crossbows Skills Choose 3: Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, Survival Class Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Focus Signature Mechanic Ranger Traps Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Focus Maximum Focus equals your PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered. once/turn One hit gains +1d6 damage and you may move 5 ft after the hit without provoking from that target. 7 Skirmisher’s Escape Reaction — Hostile ends movement within 10 ft Move up to half Speed; later improvements apply. 9 Hunter’s Rhythm Triggered / No Action — Ranged hit satisfies a listed trap, movement, or Speed condition;
