text: Level 12 — Feat / ASI Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Role Ranged weapon damage Secondary Role Mobility, precision, disruption Primary Ability DEX Secondary Ability INT Hit Die d8 Saving Throws DEX, INT Armor Leather Weapons Pistols, Muskets Signature Resource Tempo Signature Mechanic Firearm sequencing and reload rhythm Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. Tactical Shot: when a Gunslinger class feature tied to a firearm attack meaningfully forces movement, applies a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 feet of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. A single attack can never generate more than 1 normal Tempo even if it satisfies multiple conditions. Levels 1-4: normal own-turn Tempo generation is capped at 1. From Level 5: up to 2 Tempo on your own turn, but from distinct qualifying events. From Level 17: a third Tempo on your turn is possible only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Tempo never falls below 0. If you end your turn without making a Gunslinger firearm attack or successfully using a Gunslinger firearm technique, lose 1 Tempo. At Level 13 this rule improves through Sustained Tempo. Tempo Refunds A Tempo refund is not Tempo generation unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Refunds therefore do not trigger effects that require gaining Tempo. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Tempo begins at 0 in genuine combat and resets to 0 when combat ends. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. How You Gain It — Clean Hit After you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits. How You Gain It — Tactical Shot When a Gunslinger firearm technique meaningfully forces movement, imposes a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 ft of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits. Generation Limits A single attack creates at most 1 normal Tempo. Own-turn generation cap: 1 at Levels 1–4; up to 2 from Level 5 using distinct qualifying events; a third at Level 17+ only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless explicit. How You Spend It Quick Shot 1 Tempo; Deliberate Shot 1; Evasive Shot 1; Disrupting Shot 1; Pistolero Tempo

text: Level 13 Gain +1 Spell Advancement and Cadence max 6. Resonant Network: a creature is in your Resonant Network while it is within the Mantra Radius of at least one active Mantra and eligible to benefit from that Mantra. Once on each of your turns, when you successfully affect a creature in your Resonant Network with a Chanter spell or Cadence Technique, choose one additional creature in your Network within 20 feet of the original target. It gains Echoed Guard (PB temporary HP), Echoed Step (5-foot safe movement from one creature), or Echoed Resolve (+1 to its next saving throw before the start of your next turn). A creature can benefit from your Resonant Network only once per turn. Greater Cadence Flow replaces Rhythmic Recovery. Once per round, when you spend Cadence and then successfully perform a qualifying action from a different category before the start of your next turn, choose one: regain 1 Cadence; gain +10 feet Speed until the end of your next turn; or gain temporary HP equal to INT + PB until the start of your next turn.

text: Level 13 — Master Hunter and Additional Trap Ranged Striker • Focus • Traps • Tactical Repositioning Ranger “Chase me or run away. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. Tactical Shot: when a Gunslinger class feature tied to a firearm attack meaningfully forces movement, applies a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 feet of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. A single attack can never generate more than 1 normal Tempo even if it satisfies multiple conditions. Levels 1-4: normal own-turn Tempo generation is capped at 1. From Level 5: up to 2 Tempo on your own turn, but from distinct qualifying events. From Level 17: a third Tempo on your turn is possible only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Tempo never falls below 0. If you end your turn without making a Gunslinger firearm attack or successfully using a Gunslinger firearm technique, lose 1 Tempo. At Level 13 this rule improves through Sustained Tempo. text: Level 16 — Feat / ASI Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. Rune Carving: once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Rune Mark after that hit resolves. Alternatively, hitting the same creature with two different melee attacks during your turn can place 1 Rune Mark after the second hit. Normal attack-based Rune placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. Newly created Rune Marks cannot be consumed by the same hit that created them. If you exceed your current marked-target limit, choose one previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. A creature carries your Marks until they are consumed or removed. Maximum Up to 3 Rune Marks per creature. Marked-target capacity is 1 creature through Level 8, 2 from Levels 9–16, and 3 from Level 17 onward. How You Place Marks Once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Mark after the hit resolves. Alternatively, two different melee hits against the same creature during your turn can place 1 Mark after the second hit. Placement Limits Normal attack-based placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless an explicit feature increases it. A newly created Mark cannot be consumed by the hit that created it. How You Spend Them On a hit against a marked creature, Rune Burst and later Execution features consume the stated number of Marks to add Rune Dice or execution riders. Changing Targets If you exceed your marked-target capacity, choose a previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Removal / Reset Marks disappear when consumed, when the creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. Does Not Generate Missing, merely targeting, off-turn staged attacks, or hitting a creature without satisfying Rune Carving do not place Marks unless an explicit Assassin feature says otherwise. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. text: Level 18 — Perfect Firearm Mastery, Relentless Rhythm, Master Gunplay Style Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Role Ranged weapon damage Secondary Role Mobility, precision, disruption Primary Ability DEX Secondary Ability INT Hit Die d8 Saving Throws DEX, INT Armor Leather Weapons Pistols, Muskets Signature Resource Tempo Signature Mechanic Firearm sequencing and reload rhythm Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. Tactical Shot: when a Gunslinger class feature tied to a firearm attack meaningfully forces movement, applies a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 feet of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. A single attack can never generate more than 1 normal Tempo even if it satisfies multiple conditions. Levels 1-4: normal own-turn Tempo generation is capped at 1. From Level 5: up to 2 Tempo on your own turn, but from distinct qualifying events. From Level 17: a third Tempo on your turn is possible only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Tempo never falls below 0. If you end your turn without making a Gunslinger firearm attack or successfully using a Gunslinger firearm technique, lose 1 Tempo. At Level 13 this rule improves through Sustained Tempo. Tempo Refunds A Tempo refund is not Tempo generation unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Refunds therefore do not trigger effects that require gaining Tempo. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Tempo begins at 0 in genuine combat and resets to 0 when combat ends. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. How You Gain It — Clean Hit After you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits. How You Gain It — Tactical Shot When a Gunslinger firearm technique meaningfully forces movement, imposes a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 ft of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits. Generation Limits A single attack creates at most 1 normal Tempo. Own-turn generation cap: 1 at Levels 1–4; up to 2 from Level 5 using distinct qualifying events; a third at Level 17+ only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless explicit. How You Spend It Quick Shot 1 Tempo; Deliberate Shot

text: Level 18 — Unseen Predator Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. text: Level 19 — Empyrean Boon Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Role Ranged weapon damage Secondary Role Mobility, precision, disruption Primary Ability DEX Secondary Ability INT Hit Die d8 Saving Throws DEX, INT Armor Leather Weapons Pistols, Muskets Signature Resource Tempo Signature Mechanic Firearm sequencing and reload rhythm Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. Tactical Shot: when a Gunslinger class feature tied to a firearm attack meaningfully forces movement, applies a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 feet of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. A single attack can never generate more than 1 normal Tempo even if it satisfies multiple conditions. Levels 1-4: normal own-turn Tempo generation is capped at 1. From Level 5: up to 2 Tempo on your own turn, but from distinct qualifying events. From Level 17: a third Tempo on your turn is possible only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Tempo never falls below 0. If you end your turn without making a Gunslinger firearm attack or successfully using a Gunslinger firearm technique, lose 1 Tempo. At Level 13 this rule improves through Sustained Tempo. Tempo Refunds A Tempo refund is not Tempo generation unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Refunds therefore do not trigger effects that require gaining Tempo. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Tempo begins at 0 in genuine combat and resets to 0 when combat ends. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. How You Gain It — Tactical Shot When a Gunslinger firearm technique meaningfully forces movement, imposes a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 ft of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits. Generation Limits A single attack creates at most 1 normal Tempo. Own-turn generation cap: 1 at Levels 1–4; up to 2 from Level 5 using distinct qualifying events; a third at Level 17+ only from an explicitly named advanced feature. text: Level 19 — Empyrean Boon Ranged Striker • Focus • Traps • Tactical Repositioning Ranger “Chase me or run away. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d10 Saving Throws Dexterity, Strength Armor Leather Armor Weapons Longbows, Shortbows, Crossbows Skills Choose 3: Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, Survival Class Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Focus Signature Mechanic Ranger Traps Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Focus Maximum Focus equals your PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered. text: Level 2 Gain Aethertech Modules. Choose two different modules from the list below. Unless a module states otherwise, it functions only while you are piloting your Bastion. You cannot choose the same module more than once. Controlled Venting is a separate Level 2 feature and is not a module. Targeting Array. Once on each of your turns when you make an attack roll with a Bastion weapon, add +1 to that attack roll. This bonus applies to either Aether Cannon or Aether Lancer. Reinforced Plating. Increase the Bastion’s maximum HP by 2 × your Aethertech level. Recalculate this bonus whenever your Aethertech level increases. Mobility Jets. While piloting the Bastion, its Speed increases by 10 feet. In addition, once on each of your turns after you Vent Heat, you may move the Bastion 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Cooling Fins. Whenever you Vent Heat, reduce Heat by 1 additional point. This increases the normal Vent reduction from 2 to 3, and from Level 15 increases the improved Vent reduction from 3 to 4. Stabilizer Frame. While piloting the Bastion, you have Advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to resist being pushed, pulled, knocked Prone, or otherwise forcibly moved. Emergency Capacitor. Once per Short or Long Rest, when you activate an Aethertech feature that costs Aether Core and you are exactly 1 Core short of its cost, the capacitor supplies that missing 1 Core for that feature. The supplied Core exists only for that immediate cost, cannot be stored, and cannot raise your current Core above its maximum. Controlled Venting. Whenever you meaningfully Vent Heat through the Vent action or an Aethertech feature that explicitly counts as Venting, after the Heat reduction resolves choose one rider: Aetheric Pulse — one hostile creature you can see within 5 feet of the Bastion takes 1d4 Force damage; Defensive Reclamation — you gain temporary HP equal to PB + INT modifier; Thruster Reposition — move the Bastion up to 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Controlled Venting can trigger only once per Vent, and Heat reduction that merely prevents Heat gain does not count as Venting.

text: Level 2 — Gunplay Style, Tactical Reload Tempo • Firearm Rhythm • Reload Mastery • Mobile Precision Gunslinger “A bullet sounds the same to everybody.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Role Ranged weapon damage Secondary Role Mobility, precision, disruption Primary Ability DEX Secondary Ability INT Hit Die d8 Saving Throws DEX, INT Armor Leather Weapons Pistols, Muskets Signature Resource Tempo Signature Mechanic Firearm sequencing and reload rhythm Core Engine — Tempo, Firearms, and Reload The Gunslinger is a mobile firearm martial whose power comes from maintaining Tempo through successful firearm play. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Standard one-handed firearm capacity progression: Ammo Capacity 4 at Levels 1-4, Ammo Capacity 5 at 5-8, Ammo Capacity 6 at 9-14, and Ammo Capacity 7 at 15-20. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. Tactical Shot: when a Gunslinger class feature tied to a firearm attack meaningfully forces movement, applies a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 feet of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. A single attack can never generate more than 1 normal Tempo even if it satisfies multiple conditions. Levels 1-4: normal own-turn Tempo generation is capped at 1. From Level 5: up to 2 Tempo on your own turn, but from distinct qualifying events. From Level 17: a third Tempo on your turn is possible only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Tempo never falls below 0. If you end your turn without making a Gunslinger firearm attack or successfully using a Gunslinger firearm technique, lose 1 Tempo. At Level 13 this rule improves through Sustained Tempo. Tempo Refunds A Tempo refund is not Tempo generation unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Refunds therefore do not trigger effects that require gaining Tempo. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Tempo begins at 0 in genuine combat and resets to 0 when combat ends. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–12; 6 at 13–16; 7 at 17–20. How You Gain It — Clean Hit After you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits. How You Gain It — Tactical Shot When a Gunslinger firearm technique meaningfully forces movement, imposes a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 ft of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits. Generation Limits A single attack creates at most 1 normal Tempo. Own-turn generation cap: 1 at Levels 1–4; up to 2 from Level 5 using distinct qualifying events; a third at Level 17+ only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless explicit. How You Spend It Quick Shot 1 Tempo; Deliberate Shot 1; Evasive Shot 1; Disrupting Shot

Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Fire. Move. Reload. Keep the rhythm alive long enough to turn Tempo into control, defense, and lethal pressure. Class Identity Gunslingers are technist marksmen who turn Aether-assisted firearms into speed, precision, and controlled ranged pressure. Pistols support rapid, mobile sequences through Quick Shot and Akimbo, while Muskets provide deliberate two-handed fire that concentrates Tempo into stronger individual hits through Deliberate Shot. Tempo represents the Gunslinger’s ability to build combat rhythm through successful action rather than treating every shot as an isolated event. Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. The wider Aion tradition describes early firearm research being dismissed as technist tinkering until battlefield success forced major institutions to recognize the discipline. Wings of Atreia keeps that identity of innovation earning legitimacy through results while using Pistols and Muskets as the class’s only firearm categories. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability. Appearance & Adventuring Gunslingers favor mobile equipment, ammunition management, firearm maintenance, and a practical awareness of range and firing position. Their weapons can make them look strikingly modern beside older martial traditions, but their discipline remains Aetheric and distinctly Atreian. They adventure to test new techniques, serve as ranged specialists, hunt dangerous targets, protect expeditions from positions others cannot exploit, or demonstrate that innovation has earned its place in the war for Atreia. Firearms are class-supported Gunslinger weapons; carrying two firearms does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols Ranged Gunslinger One-handed Weapon Attack. Range 30/90 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d8 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. A Gunslinger can wield two Pistols, but doing so does not itself grant extra attacks. Pistols are compatible with Quick Shot and Akimbo. Muskets Ranged Gunslinger Two-handed Weapon Attack. Range 60/180 feet. Attack modifier = PB + DEX. On a hit, deal 1d12 + DEX modifier Piercing damage. Ammunition capacity is fixed at 2. Muskets cannot use Quick Shot or Akimbo. Gunslinger ammunition-restoration features can restore Musket shots normally, but a Musket can never hold more than 2 shots. Standard one-handed firearm capacity increases do not apply to Muskets. Reload Every firearm attack consumes one shot. A firearm with no shots remaining is Empty and cannot make firearm attacks until at least one shot is restored. Normal Bonus Action Reload: an Empty firearm is restored to its full Reload capacity. Ammunition restoration is not the Reload action unless a feature explicitly says so. Ammunition-restoration features can restore shots to either Pistols or Muskets up to that firearm's maximum capacity. A Musket's maximum capacity remains 2. Switching between carried one-handed Gunslinger firearms as part of a firearm attack requires no separate object interaction. Increasing capacity does not automatically reload an Empty firearm. Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. Maximum Tempo: Levels 1-4 = 3; 5-8 = 4; 9-12 = 5; 13-16 = 6; 17-20 = 7. Clean Hit: after you hit a hostile creature with a Gunslinger firearm attack, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. Tactical Shot: when a Gunslinger class feature tied to a firearm attack meaningfully forces movement, applies a meaningful hostile penalty, or creates at least 5 feet of safe movement, gain 1 Tempo, subject to the generation limits below. A single attack can never generate more than 1 normal Tempo even if it satisfies multiple conditions. Levels 1-4: normal own-turn Tempo generation is capped at 1. From Level 5: up to 2 Tempo on your own turn, but from distinct qualifying events. From Level 17: a third Tempo on your turn is possible only from an explicitly named advanced feature. Outside your turn, gain at most 1 Tempo per round unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Tempo never falls below 0. If you end your turn without making a Gunslinger firearm attack or successfully using a Gunslinger firearm technique, lose 1 Tempo. At Level 13 this rule improves through Sustained Tempo. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. text: Level 4 — Feat / Ability Score Improvement Melee Striker • Sneak Attack • Rune Marks • Execution Assassin “You'll know I'm there when you're dead.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Assassin is a precision melee striker that builds target-bound Rune Marks, converts them into burst damage or execution riders, and uses Shadow Step to remain difficult to pin down. Unlike a conventional Extra Attack martial, its Level 5 Assassination Sequence is a conditional follow-up attack tied to a successful Sneak Attack. Class Identity Assassins are precision predators who win through positioning, timing, concealment, and carefully prepared execution. Their art is not simply “attacking from stealth.” An Assassin studies a target, creates the right opening, carves Rune Marks, and converts preparation into a sudden lethal advantage. Their greatest strength is the ability to decide where and when a close-range confrontation becomes dangerous. Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique. Appearance & Adventuring Assassins favor equipment that permits mobility and unobstructed movement, with Shortswords and Daggers forming the class’s approved weapon identity in Wings of Atreia. Their appearance may be subdued or ceremonial, but practical Assassins avoid anything that compromises movement or control. They adventure when a threat must be found before it strikes, a route must be infiltrated, an enemy leader must be neutralized, or a mystery demands someone comfortable operating unseen. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Constitution Hit Die d8 Saving Throws Dexterity, Intelligence Armor Leather Armor Weapons Shortswords, Daggers Skills Choose 3: Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Stealth Class Save DC 8 + PB + DEX modifier Signature Resource Rune Marks placed on enemies Signature Mechanics Sneak Attack, Rune Carving, Rune Burst, Shadow Step Extra Attack No standard Extra Attack; Assassination Sequence at Level 5 Spellcasting None Core Engine — Sneak Attack and Rune Marks Sneak Attack applies once on each of your own turns when an eligible finesse melee weapon attack has Advantage, or when another qualifying enemy is adjacent to the target and you do not have Disadvantage. Sneak Attack damage scales from 1d6 at Level 1 to 10d6 at Level 19. Levels Sneak Attack Rune Die Marked Targets 1–2 1d6 d4 1 3–4 2d6 d4 1 5–6 3d6 d6 1 7–8 4d6 d6 1 9–10 5d6 d6 2 11–12 6d6 d8 2 13–14 7d6 d8 2 15–16 8d6 d8 2 17–18 9d6 d10 3 19–20 10d6 d10 3 A creature can carry up to 3 of your Rune Marks. Rune Carving: once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Rune Mark after that hit resolves. Alternatively, hitting the same creature with two different melee attacks during your turn can place 1 Rune Mark after the second hit. Normal attack-based Rune placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. Newly created Rune Marks cannot be consumed by the same hit that created them. If you exceed your current marked-target limit, choose one previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Marks disappear when consumed, when the marked creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Resource Form Rune Marks are target-bound counters, not a generic personal pool. A creature carries your Marks until they are consumed or removed. Maximum Up to 3 Rune Marks per creature. Marked-target capacity is 1 creature through Level 8, 2 from Levels 9–16, and 3 from Level 17 onward. How You Place Marks Once on your turn, a qualifying melee hit that actually deals Sneak Attack places 1 Mark after the hit resolves. Alternatively, two different melee hits against the same creature during your turn can place 1 Mark after the second hit. Placement Limits Normal attack-based placement is limited to 1 Mark per turn unless an explicit feature increases it. A newly created Mark cannot be consumed by the hit that created it. How You Spend Them On a hit against a marked creature, Rune Burst and later Execution features consume the stated number of Marks to add Rune Dice or execution riders. Changing Targets If you exceed your marked-target capacity, choose a previously marked creature and remove all of your Marks from it. Removal / Reset Marks disappear when consumed, when the creature is defeated, or when the encounter ends. Does Not Generate Missing, merely targeting, off-turn staged attacks, or hitting a creature without satisfying Rune Carving do not place Marks unless an explicit Assassin feature says otherwise. text: Level 4 — Feat / Ability Score Improvement Ranged Striker • Focus • Traps • Tactical Repositioning Ranger “Chase me or run away. Either way, you'll only die tired.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequences Specialization Reassignment The Ranger is a nonmagical ranged hunter that controls enemy movement with persistent battlefield traps, spends Focus on precision or evasive shots, and is rewarded for exploiting targets that walk into prepared terrain. Its sustained damage comes from two ranged attacks, not from spellcasting or a third standard attack. Class Identity Rangers are mobile ranged specialists who control distance through marksmanship, movement, traps, and battlefield awareness. They are most effective when they can read terrain before committing, choose favorable lines of attack, and punish enemies that approach carelessly. Focus represents the Ranger’s ability to convert patience and perception into precise action. Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. Rangers are common among scouts, hunters, pathfinders, border wardens, reconnaissance troops, and independent Daevas accustomed to surviving beyond secure settlements. They tend to value preparedness, observation, mobility, and freedom of movement. Appearance & Adventuring Rangers usually wear mobile armor and carry bows, ammunition, traps, and field equipment suited to extended movement. Their gear often reflects the terrain in which they learned their craft. Rangers adventure to explore dangerous regions, hunt monsters or enemy operatives, guide expeditions, secure routes, protect remote communities, or prove that no battlefield is truly open ground when preparation and range are on their side. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Dexterity Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d10 Saving Throws Dexterity, Strength Armor Leather Armor Weapons Longbows, Shortbows, Crossbows Skills Choose 3: Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, Survival Class Save DC 8 + PB + WIS modifier Signature Resource Focus Signature Mechanic Ranger Traps Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Focus Maximum Focus equals your PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Focus. A Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Focus is a tactical reserve rather than ammunition or a tax on ordinary ranged attacks; Ranger Traps normally cost no Focus. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Focus is a rest-based reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + WIS modifier, minimum 2. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. Combat Recovery Hunter’s Rhythm and certain later Ranger/specialization features can regain Focus during genuine combat when their tactical conditions are actually satisfied. How You Spend It Precision Shot 1 Focus; Pinning Shot 1 Focus; Evasive Step 1 Focus; Deadeye Perfect Shot 1 Focus. Other Ranger features spend Focus only when their text states a cost. Refunds / Recovery A combat refund or recovery is not a new attack, trap trigger, or separate technique. It simply restores Focus up to your maximum. Persistence Unused Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored; there is no automatic combat-end reset. Does Not Generate Standing still and firing, harmless staged interactions, or ordinary trap placement do not create Focus unless an explicit recovery feature is actually triggered.
