text: Rest, Hit Dice, Exhaustion & Survival Player Rules Combat Turn structure, actions, movement, attacks, damage, conditions, death, rests, and survival. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative Round and Turn Action Economy Attack Action Universal Actions Ready Turn Structure & Actions Genuine Combat Initiative, rounds, and combat-only resources are used only for genuine combat or another situation where structured turn order is necessary. Characters cannot manufacture artificial combat to farm cooldowns, resources, or timing triggers. Initiative Initiative = 1d20 + Dexterity modifier. Do not add PB unless an explicit feature says so. Alert adds +2 Initiative. There is no Surprise Round and Surprise does not grant Advantage on Initiative. When one side genuinely catches another side unaware, the GM may, at discretion, allow one appropriate pre-Initiative attack roll against the target's normal defense before Initiative is rolled. This is not an extra round, is not automatic, and does not create a general Surprise action economy. After that resolution, roll Initiative normally. Round and Turn One combat round represents approximately six seconds in the game world. Each participant normally takes one turn in Initiative order. All turns in the round abstract actions occurring within the same six-second span; do not add each turn as another six seconds. Action Economy Action. One per turn. Movement. Up to the creature’s available movement, subject to terrain and conditions. Bonus Action. Up to one, but only when a feature grants something that uses a Bonus Action. Reaction. Normally one per round, refreshing at the start of the creature’s turn unless an explicit class rule says otherwise. Object interaction. One free simple object interaction per turn. There is no universal Action-to-Bonus-Action or Bonus-Action-to-Action conversion. Unused movement or Actions are not stored for later turns. Attack Action The Attack Action makes one attack unless a feature such as Extra Attack says otherwise. Grapple and Shove are full Actions and do not replace one attack within Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. A player character must be wielding an approved class weapon to take the normal Attack Action. Unarmed Attacks and Improvised Weapons are not player combat options unless a later explicit feature creates a specific exception. Opportunity Attacks. Opportunity Attacks remain part of the core combat rules. When a hostile creature you can perceive voluntarily leaves your melee reach, you may use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it, resolving the attack before it leaves that reach. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Universal Actions Dash. Gain additional movement equal to your current Speed for the turn. Difficult Terrain and other movement costs still apply. While flying, Dash adds horizontal movement but does not grant an additional altitude-layer change. Disengage. Until the end of your turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Dodge. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have Disadvantage if you can perceive the attacker, and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. Dodge ends if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0. Hide. You must have meaningful concealment or another circumstance that allows hiding. Make Dexterity (Stealth) against Passive Perception or active Perception as appropriate. You cannot Hide while clearly seen. Hidden is not Invisible. Making an attack reveals your position after that attack resolves. Search. Deliberately search using a GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation). Use Object. Use this Action for substantial manipulation beyond the one free simple object interaction. A specific item’s activation rule controls when it states another cost. Ready A creature can prepare one Action for a perceivable trigger. When the trigger occurs, the creature may use its Reaction to perform the readied Action. Ready does not store ordinary movement, but Dash can be readied as the Action. Readied attacks retain all weapon properties. A readied spell must still meet implement and targeting requirements when released. Losing a mandatory implement before release prevents release. Concentration begins when the spell actually resolves. Ready never bypasses aerial restrictions, range, or other universal rules. Simultaneous Effects Effects resolve one at a time. The active creature orders its own simultaneous effects; the GM orders GM-controlled simultaneous effects. For opposing same-time effects, resolve the active creature first, then use Initiative if needed. Damage resolves before state changes caused by that damage. Start-of-turn and end-of-turn timing is literal. Reactions follow their trigger wording and are not inserted retroactively after the consequence has already resolved unless a rule explicitly allows it. Movement, Positioning & Physical Interaction Ground Movement Base Walk. 30 feet for a Daeva unless modified. Difficult Terrain. Costs 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot traveled. Prone. Standing from Prone requires one full Action and does not consume movement. A creature can move normally afterward if movement remains available. No universal Flanking. Opposite sides do not automatically grant Advantage. No universal Facing. Being behind a creature does not automatically grant Advantage. Occupied Spaces. A creature may move through a willing allied creature's space, treating that space as difficult terrain unless an explicit feature says otherwise. A creature cannot move through an enemy or neutral creature's occupied space unless an explicit rule permits it, and cannot end movement in another creature's occupied space unless an explicit rule allows it. Grapple and Shove Grapple and Shove each require a full Action. The target must be within reach and no more than one Size larger than you. Make Strength (Athletics) contested by the target’s choice of Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics). On a successful Grapple, the target becomes Grappled; it may use its Action to escape by repeating the contest. Moving a Grappled creature costs 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot moved unless the target is at least two Sizes smaller than you. On a successful Shove, choose to push the target 5 feet or knock it Prone. Grapple and Shove do not replace attacks within the Attack Action and cannot substitute for Extra Attack. Player Weapon Requirement. Player characters do not use a universal Unarmed Attack damage rule; the normal Attack Action requires an approved class weapon unless an explicit feature says otherwise. Specializations — Read Before You Choose Assassin chooses an initial Specialization at Level 3. Use this preview before reading the Level 1–20 progression so you can see the playstyle each path develops into. Specialization features are gained at Levels 3, 6, 10, and 14. Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Executioner Runemark burst finisher Pushes Assassination Sequence toward harder full-pattern executions, stronger critical windows, and lethal wounded-target finishers. Best for players who want precise setup followed by decisive burst. Phantom Stealth and repositioning assassin Improves Shadow Step, hiding, movement around Assassination Sequence, and temporary invisibility. Best for players who want evasive hit-and-fade play and positional control. Nightstalker Quarry hunter and pursuer Marks and tracks a chosen quarry, resists concealment tricks, and pursues enemies that try to escape. Best for players who want relentless single-target pressure and pursuit. Specialization Advancement Preview Level Executioner Phantom Nightstalker 3 Deep Carving — full three-Mark cash-out +1 Rune Die. Vanishing Step — improved Shadow Step plus free Hide attempt. Hunter’s Rune — quarry tracking and stronger anti-Hide. 6 Execution Window — 19–20 full-pattern crit. Fleeting Shadow — move before/after Assassination Sequence. Relentless Quarry — Reaction pursuit of willing movement. 10 Lingering Ruin — survivor receives 1 replacement Mark. Veiled Passage — successful Vanishing Step Hide grants temporary Invisible. True Quarry — 120-ft tracking and 60-ft quarry Aether Trace. 14 Death Sentence — wounded full execution crit 18–20. Perfect Vanishing — full cash-out grants temporary Invisible. No Escape — Reaction Ghost Pursuit follows movement or teleport. Specialization Reassignment Initial choice — Level 3. Choose one Specialization available to your class. Reassignment checkpoints — Levels 6, 10, and 14. When gaining one of these levels, you may either continue your current Specialization or change to another Specialization available to your class. If you change Specialization, remove every feature granted by the previous Specialization and replace it with the complete feature package of the newly selected Specialization through your current checkpoint . Features from different Specializations cannot be mixed, retained, or combined. When newly entering a Specialization, make any choices required by the features you now gain. Continuing the same Specialization does not reset earlier internal choices unless an explicit feature says otherwise. If the removed Specialization granted extra known options, selections, capacities, or Specialization-dependent maxima, remove, reselect, or recalculate them as necessary to satisfy the new path. Reassignment itself does not restore HP or class resources, and current values cannot remain above any new maximum. Reassignment occurs only as part of gaining Level 6, Level 10, or Level 14 . It cannot be performed through a rest, downtime, training, ordinary retraining, or between adventures. The Level 14 decision is the final normal Specialization choice and remains locked through Level 20 unless a later explicit rule says otherwise.

text: Sanctum Sanctum is the monumental floating capital of Elysea, suspended above Oriel and visible as one of the great symbols of Elyos civilization. Its luminous plazas, temples, government halls, Legion offices, archives, and scholarly institutions make it a center of civic life as much as military power. The city was raised during the long southern reconstruction after the Cataclysm rather than surviving unchanged from ancient Atreia. Public ceremony, learning, art, diplomacy, and service all contribute to the capital’s cultivated identity. For Elyos Daevas, Sanctum is where victories become policy, discoveries enter archives, and service to Elysea can draw the attention of powerful institutions. Most civic areas are orderly and accessible, while military compounds, temple spaces, and restricted records remain controlled. Adventures here tend toward investigation, diplomacy, political consequences, research, or threats hidden beneath the security of the capital. Sanctum represents what Elyos society believes it rebuilt from the ruin of the old world.

Subjects can include history, geography, creatures, Aether, ruins, cultures, warfare, or any other serious field of inquiry. Motivations and Outlook. A Scholar may adventure to recover lost knowledge, investigate mysteries, study ruins or creatures directly, protect important discoveries, or prevent dangerous knowledge from being misused. Playing a Scholar. Choose the subject that fascinates you and decide whether you are an academic, a practical field researcher, or something between. Being scholarly does not require being socially awkward or confined to books.

text: Selling and Disposal Selling requires a plausible buyer. The GM determines value; there is no universal resale percentage. Consider quality, condition, rarity, local demand, location, faction access, and ownership. The ability to sell an item does not imply that category is ordinarily purchasable. Aether gear can be sold but does not return its Refined Aether as a universal salvage rule. Legendary items have no ordinary market price. Cosmetic Wings can be sold for GM-determined value. Damaged items sell at a discount; Destroyed items are salvage at best. Stolen goods may create consequences. There is no repeated buyer-reroll loop or assumption of infinite merchant liquidity. Bosses and Lords. Every ordinary Boss-rank monster uses Boss Actions as defined in its statblock. Empyrean and Dragon Lords use Lord Actions. Boss Action and Lord Action are distinct official Wings of Atreia mechanical terms; Legendary Action is not. ← Back to Rules

text: Services, Persistence, and Commerce An Active Profession user may perform Profession work for another character; the recipient does not need the Profession. Completed Profession results remain valid if the practitioner later changes Profession. Equipment quality stays attached to the item through transfer, trade, sale, or new ownership. NPC practitioners may provide the same services as PCs of the same rank and must obey the same rank, material, facility, work-time, sequential-upgrade, and other core requirements. text: Shared Aether Once on each of your turns when you cast a Spiritmaster spell that affects a hostile creature within 10 feet of your spirit, choose one: Channel Through Spirit measures range, origin, cover, and line of effect from the spirit’s space while you remain the caster; or Resonant Target gives +1 to the spell attack or +1 to the first save DC against one creature adjacent to your spirit. Self-range spells cannot normally be projected through the spirit. Specializations — Read Before You Choose Spiritmaster chooses an initial Specialization at Level 3. Use this preview before reading the Level 1–20 progression so you can see the playstyle each path develops into. Specialization features are gained at Levels 3, 6, 10, and 14. Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Spirit Caller Empowered spirit specialist Strengthens the summoned spirit’s offense, persistence, and eventual ascendance. Best for players who want their spirit companion to be the centerpiece of their combat plan. Hexbinder Curse and debuff specialist Extends and compounds hostile hexes so enemies suffer deeper and more persistent penalties. Best for players who enjoy weakening key targets and controlling fights through curses. Bondweaver Spirit-bond efficiency specialist Deepens the bond between Spiritmaster and spirit, improving efficiency, resilience, shared protection, and resource flow. Best for players who want a durable and flexible partnership with their spirit. Specialization Advancement Preview Level Spirit Caller Hexbinder Bondweaver 3 Empowered Spirit; Predatory Bond Lingering Hex; Cursed Conduit Deepened Bond; Efficient Bond; Shared Guard 6 Relentless Spirit Malignant Echo Resonant Bond 10 Spirit Ascendance Compounding Hex Overflowing Bond 14 Apex Spirit Dominion Hex Perfect Resonance Specialization Reassignment Initial choice — Level 3. Choose one Specialization available to your class. Reassignment checkpoints — Levels 6, 10, and 14. When gaining one of these levels, you may either continue your current Specialization or change to another Specialization available to your class. If you change Specialization, remove every feature granted by the previous Specialization and replace it with the complete feature package of the newly selected Specialization through your current checkpoint . Features from different Specializations cannot be mixed, retained, or combined. When newly entering a Specialization, make any choices required by the features you now gain. Continuing the same Specialization does not reset earlier internal choices unless an explicit feature says otherwise. If the removed Specialization granted extra known options, selections, capacities, or Specialization-dependent maxima, remove, reselect, or recalculate them as necessary to satisfy the new path. Reassignment itself does not restore HP or class resources, and current values cannot remain above any new maximum. Reassignment occurs only as part of gaining Level 6, Level 10, or Level 14 . It cannot be performed through a rest, downtime, training, ordinary retraining, or between adventures. The Level 14 decision is the final normal Specialization choice and remains locked through Level 20 unless a later explicit rule says otherwise.

No single modern faction controls the whole network, and knowledge of
text: Silentera Canyon Silentera Canyon is a vast physical subterranean network of canyons, tunnels, chambers, ruins, and hidden routes linking the Inggison and Gelkmaros frontiers. It is neither a Rift network nor a separate dimension; Daevas enter an actual deep fracture system beneath the Balaurean frontier. No single modern faction controls the whole network, and knowledge of one mapped corridor does not imply knowledge of every branch. Beshmundir Temple is the greatest known deep site associated with these routes. For expeditionary Daevas, Silentera is a place of uncertain maps, ambushes, sealed ruins, difficult escape routes, and encounters where Elyos and Asmodian interests may collide far from reinforcement. Guides may know particular passages without understanding the entire system, while deeper areas remain contested, Balaur-dominated, or simply unexplored. The canyon supports dungeon exploration, rescue, espionage, archaeology, and situations where temporary cooperation can become more useful than faction pride. Every descent should reinforce the feeling that the known frontier is only a narrow opening into a much larger outer world.

Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of
text: Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Player Rules Exploration & Interaction Vision, stealth, traps, locks, theft, hazards, social rules, chases, and loot. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's player-facing rules and terminology. Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect Stealth and Infiltration Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Locks Theft and Pickpocket Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Vision, Stealth, Traps, Locks & Theft Vision and Light Light states are Bright Light, Dim Light, and Darkness. Obscuration states are Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured. Dim Light lightly obscures; Darkness heavily obscures a creature that cannot otherwise see through it. Daeva Darkvision treats Darkness within 60 feet as Dim Light, not Bright Light. A recommended ordinary light source has a stated Bright radius plus an equal additional Dim radius unless its own text says otherwise. Bright light does not universally prohibit Stealth. Obscurity and Invisibility do not automatically make a creature Hidden. Cover, Line of Sight & Line of Effect No Cover. No defensive benefit from Cover. Half Cover. A creature or object behind meaningful partial obstruction gains +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects originating from the covered direction. Intervening creatures can provide Half Cover when they materially obstruct the line. Full Cover. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and prevents direct targeting through that obstruction unless an explicit rule says otherwise. Three-Quarters Cover does not exist in Wings of Atreia. Cover does not stack; use the best applicable Cover. Altitude neither inherently grants nor ignores Cover. Line of Sight and Line of Effect are distinct. Line of Sight determines whether you can see a target or point. Line of Effect determines whether an attack, spell, or effect can physically reach it. Heavy obscurement is not Cover by itself. Stealth and Infiltration Use scene states Undetected, Suspicious, and Alerted; these are not Conditions. Stealth must exceed Passive Perception; ties favor the observer. An active Search uses the GM-selected check, commonly Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation), against the relevant DC or opposing Stealth; ties favor the Searcher where opposed. Do not reroll Stealth every 5 feet; roll again only when circumstances materially change. For group Stealth, at least half the group must succeed. A failed check may create Suspicion rather than immediate full alarm when appropriate. Distractions create an opportunity to Hide rather than automatic success. Disguises are primarily social. Invisibility is not the same as Hidden. Wings do not automatically prevent Stealth. Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation. Disable methods depend on the mechanism and can use Sleight of Hand, Investigation, Athletics, or another appropriate Skill. There is no mandatory Thieves’ Tools system. Failure triggers the hazard only when the hazard says so. Damage and Conditions use existing universal rules. Forced movement is horizontal unless the hazard explicitly creates vertical displacement. Hazards normally resolve when triggered rather than taking their own Initiative turns. Repeat attempts require changed circumstances. Locks Mechanical Lock DC Simple 10 Standard 12 Secure 15 High Security 18 Exceptional 20+ The correct key opens a normal lock without a check. Mechanical locks generally use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). Unusual mechanisms can use Intelligence (Investigation). Forcing uses Strength (Athletics); destroying a lock or door uses normal object/destruction adjudication. Failure does not automatically break or trigger a lock unless its design says so. Aether locks use Aether Interaction. If a task is impossible, do not assign an absurd DC—state that it cannot be done by that method. Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances. Social Interaction, Information & Captivity Attitudes NPC attitudes are Friendly, Neutral, or Hostile. Roleplay comes first; a roll is used only when outcome and consequence are uncertain. Common skills include Persuasion, Deception, Intimidation, Insight, and Investigation. Plausibility A social check cannot force an impossible concession or make an NPC believe something fundamentally implausible without exceptional circumstances. Leverage affects what is possible and can influence DCs, but it does not automatically grant Advantage. Interrogation An interrogated NPC can reveal only information they actually know. Resolve one meaningful line of questioning at a time. Failure may close that approach, create resistance, or produce consequences; repeated checks need changed circumstances. Insight is not mind reading. Deception may oppose Insight when appropriate. Intimidation can succeed while still creating later consequences. Information Gathering Information comes from plausible sources. Common knowledge needs no roll. Use the skill that matches the approach. Rumors may be Reliable, Uncertain, or False, but the GM does not label them for the players. Independent sources and evidence can verify claims. Restricted information requires access. There is no fixed universal gathering-time formula and no check spam. Captivity and Restraints Physical restraints use Restrained when their actual effect warrants it. Binding an unwilling conscious creature in combat requires control first and normally an Action. Escape can use Sleight of Hand, Athletics, or Acrobatics against the restraint’s DC. A locked cell does not automatically impose Restrained. Restrained does not inherently prevent spellcasting, but implement and action requirements still matter. Ordinary restraints do not suppress Wings, Aetheric Reconstitution, or class powers unless an explicit specialized restraint says so. Transporting prisoners uses ordinary logistics. Interrogation remains a separate social procedure. Chases, Morale, Escorts & Creature Transport Chases Band Approximate Separation Enga

text: Soldier What Is a Soldier?. A Soldier has meaningful experience with organized military service: troops, guards, scouts, officers, fortress personnel, or other disciplined fighting forces. title: Songweaver
desc: Complete player reference for the Songweaver class in Wings of Atreia, based on Player Handbook v3.10.
text: Full Caster • Song Roles • Refrains • Resonance Songweaver “Here's a note you won't forget.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Songweaver has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Songweaver Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Performance Sequence Tradition & Outlook Specialization Reassignment The Songweaver changes battlefield purpose from moment to moment. Every Songweaver spell belongs to Harmony, Guard, Dissonance, or Requiem. Successful performances create short-lived Refrains, changing Song Roles builds Resonance, and Resonance is spent to amplify, sustain, counter, or conduct the performance. Class Identity Songweavers shape Aether through music, using performance as destructive spellcraft, support, control, and restoration. Their strength lies in versatility: the same class can pressure an enemy, sustain an ally, or shift the emotional and tactical rhythm of an encounter. Resonance represents the accumulating harmony between performance, spellcraft, and the unfolding battle. Tradition & Outlook The Songweaver tradition is rooted in Atreia’s Muses and in remembrance of Siel. The wider Aion tradition describes Muses who continued their studies after the Cataclysm and eventually joined music with Aether in service to their people; their battlefield contribution led to recognition as an established Daeva class. Songweavers may therefore approach performance as remembrance, artistry, scholarship, service, or a declaration that beauty still has power in a broken world. Appearance & Adventuring Songweavers use Lutes and Lyres as their approved implements, often making instrument, costume, gesture, and magical display part of a single visible identity. Their appearance can range from formal performer to traveling battle-musician without changing class mechanics. They adventure to preserve stories, honor Siel, inspire allies, master Aetheric music, carry culture into war-torn regions, or use beauty and sound as weapons against forces that would reduce Atreia to silence. Harmonic Support A single Songweaver spell meaningfully benefits two or more creatures. Dissonant Performance A single Songweaver spell meaningfully affects two or more hostile creatures. Contrasting Verse The successfully cast Songweaver spell uses a Song Role different from your previous successful Song Role. The first successful role in combat only establishes role history. Generation Limits Each condition triggers at most once per casting, and a casting still produces only the amount permitted by the current per-turn generation cap. Normal base generation is capped at 1 Resonance per turn unless a feature explicitly increases it. Secondary Refrain/Chorus/rider effects do not recursively generate Resonance. Resonance resets to 0 when combat ends. title: Sorcerer
desc: Complete player reference for the Sorcerer class in Wings of Atreia, based on Player Handbook v3.10.
text: Full Caster • Elemental Damage • Aether Focus • Spell Shaping Sorcerer “This will only hurt for a second.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Sorcerer has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Sorcerer Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Aether Focus Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Spellcasting Example Specialization Reassignment The Sorcerer is the raw magical-damage benchmark. It casts through Fire, Ice, Lightning, and Wind spell chains, then spends Aether Focus only when a particular spell needs more damage, area, control pressure, or reliability. Aether Focus enhances spells; it is never the fuel required to cast ordinary Sorcerer spells. Class Identity Sorcerers are masters of direct Aetheric spellcraft, combining destructive magic with the ability to control the shape and tempo of a fight. They can punish clustered enemies, deny movement or action, and unleash powerful spells when an opening appears. Aether Focus represents the concentration and arcane discipline required to turn immense magical potential into reliable battlefield power. Tradition & Outlook The Sorcerer tradition grows from Atreia’s mage disciplines and is associated with formal magical study, experimentation, academies, battlefield arcanists, and Daevas fascinated by the structure of Aether itself. Sorcerers commonly value knowledge, precision, preparation, and intellectual mastery, although their personalities range from scholarly restraint to spectacular confidence. For many, magic is both a weapon and a language through which Atreia can be understood. Appearance & Adventuring Sorcerers favor cloth armor and magical implements such as Orbs and Spellbooks under the Wings of Atreia equipment rules. Their appearance may reflect academic, military, ceremonial, or highly individual magical traditions. They adventure to recover lost knowledge, study Aetheric phenomena, test magical theories, defend their people with overwhelming spellcraft, or confront powers that ordinary weapons cannot adequately answer. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Ability Intelligence Secondary Ability Wisdom Hit Die d6 Saving Throws Constitution, Intelligence Armor Cloth Implements Magical Orbs, Spellbooks Spellcasting Ability INT Spell Save DC 8 + PB + INT modifier Spell Attack PB + INT modifier Signature Resource Aether Focus Spell Advancements +2 every class level after 1; 38 total Maximum Spell Level 9 Extra Attack None Core Engine — Aether Focus Maximum Aether Focus equals PB + INT modifier, minimum 2. A Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. A Short Rest restores Aether Focus equal to PB, up to your maximum. The resource is an enhancement reserve: casting an ordinary Sorcerer spell never requires Aether Focus unless a spell or class feature explicitly says otherwise. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Aether Focus is a rest-based enhancement reserve and does not reset merely because combat begins or ends. After a Long Rest it is normally full. Maximum PB + INT modifier, minimum 2. Aether Sage and the Level 20 capstone can explicitly increase this maximum. Rest Recovery Long Rest restores all expended Aether Focus. Short Rest restores Focus equal to PB, up to maximum; Aether Sage can improve this recovery. Base Generation The base Sorcerer does not generate Aether Focus from ordinary spell hits or damage. Combat refunds exist only where a class or specialization feature explicitly grants them. How You Spend It Intensify 1 Focus; Widen 1 Focus; Potent Control 1 Focus; other Sorcerer features spend Aether Focus only when their text states a cost. Ordinary spellcasting costs no Focus. Refunds / Discounts Aether Sage and later features may discount a shaping cost or refund Focus after a qualifying shaped spell. A refund is not a second casting or a new spell trigger. Persistence Unused Aether Focus persists between encounters until spent or restored. Important Distinction Aether Focus is a Sorcerer class resource. It is not environmental Aether, Refined Aether, an Aether State, or a universal damage type. text: Specialization Advancement Preview Level Virtuoso Muse Dirgekeeper 3 Piercing Refrain; Crescendo Forte Shared Harmony; Protective Cadence Lingering Discord; Broken Measure 6 Flourishing Requiem; Resonant Overtones Shared Melody; Gentle Reprise Crushing Discord; Echo of Failure 10 Shattering Reprise; Virtuoso Momentum Harmonic Shelter; Restorative Echo Dissonant Suppression; Deep Discord 14 Grand Requiem; Final Flourish Grand Chorus; Perfect Reprise Grand Dirge; Feeding Discord Specialization Reassignment Initial choice — Level 3. Choose one Specialization available to your class. Reassignment checkpoints — Levels 6, 10, and 14. When gaining one of these levels, you may either continue your current Specialization or change to another Specialization available to your class. If you change Specialization, remove every feature granted by the previous Specialization and replace it with the complete feature package of the newly selected Specialization through your current checkpoint . Features from different Specializations cannot be mixed, retained, or combined. When newly entering a Specialization, make any choices required by the features you now gain. Continuing the same Specialization does not reset earlier internal choices unless an explicit feature says otherwise. If the removed Specialization granted extra known options, selections, capacities, or Specialization-dependent maxima, remove, reselect, or recalculate them as necessary to satisfy the new path. Reassignment itself does not restore HP or class resources, and current values cannot remain above any new maximum. Reassignment occurs only as part of gaining Level 6, Level 10, or Level 14 . It cannot be performed through a rest, downtime, training, ordinary retraining, or between adventures. The Level 14 decision is the final normal Specialization choice and remains locked through Level 20 unless a later explicit rule says otherwise.

text: Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Siege Engineer Heavy-cannon artillery specialist Builds Aether Core and manages Heat to deliver the class’s strongest cannon bursts and siege pressure. Best for players who want deliberate setup followed by powerful ranged payoff. Bulwark Pilot Defensive Bastion specialist Strengthens Bastion durability, mitigation, interception, and protective positioning. Best for players who want to keep the combat platform standing and shield allies from pressure. Flux Engineer Core-and-Heat systems specialist Manipulates Aether Core and Heat more flexibly, converting resources and exploiting Pressurized states while controlling Overheat. Best for players who enjoy resource management and adaptable system play.

text: Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Executioner Runemark burst finisher Pushes Assassination Sequence toward harder full-pattern executions, stronger critical windows, and lethal wounded-target finishers. Best for players who want precise setup followed by decisive burst. Phantom Stealth and repositioning assassin Improves Shadow Step, hiding, movement around Assassination Sequence, and temporary invisibility. Best for players who want evasive hit-and-fade play and positional control. Nightstalker Quarry hunter and pursuer Marks and tracks a chosen quarry, resists concealment tricks, and pursues enemies that try to escape. Best for players who want relentless single-target pressure and pursuit.

text: Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect War Chanter Martial cadence specialist Turns Cadence into a more aggressive battle rhythm, improving martial flow, sustained assault, and combat pressure. Best for players who want the Chanter to fight closer to the front line. Harmonic Sage Mantra and support specialist Expands Mantra efficiency, harmony, shared benefits, and supportive Cadence use. Best for players who want the strongest emphasis on party support and sustained utility. Dissonant Voice Disruption and debuff specialist Uses Dissonance to weaken enemies, punish failed defenses, and deepen disruptive effects. Best for players who want support through enemy suppression rather than direct protection.

text: Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Healer Restoration specialist Strengthens direct healing, overflow restoration, emergency recovery, and life-saving output. text: Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Deadeye Patient precision archer Rewards controlled positioning, careful aim, cover penetration, and powerful finishing shots. text: Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Virtuoso Offensive performance specialist Pushes musical magic toward stronger refrains, requiems, crescendos, and damaging finales. text: Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Elementalist Devoted elemental specialist Commits to Fire, Ice, or Lightning and progressively strengthens that element’s damage or control rider. Best for players who want a strong elemental identity and straightforward spell pressure. Spellbinder Arcane control specialist Adds seals, area manipulation, Concentration protection, and increasingly firm constraints on enemy movement and reactions. text: Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Spirit Caller Empowered spirit specialist Strengthens the summoned spirit’s offense, persistence, and eventual ascendance. Best for players who want their spirit companion to be the centerpiece of their combat plan. Hexbinder Curse and debuff specialist Extends and compounds hostile hexes so enemies suffer deeper and more persistent penalties. Best for players who enjoy weakening key targets and controlling fights through curses. Bondweaver Spirit-bond efficiency specialist Deepens the bond between Spiritmaster and spirit, improving efficiency, resilience, shared protection, and resource flow. Best for players who want a durable and flexible partnership with their spirit.

text: Specialization Preview Specialization Identity What You Can Expect Bulwark Interception and ally protection Improves Guardian’s Intercession, shared Resolve, emergency saves, and resistance while taking danger meant for allies. Best for players who want the strongest bodyguard identity. Justicar Challenge and retaliation defender Punishes enemies for defying Challenge through stronger reactions, control, and judgment. Best for players who want defense that actively threatens enemies who ignore them. Aegis Space-control defender Turns nearby space into difficult, punishing ground and increasingly prevents enemies from moving through your reach. Best for players who want to hold chokepoints and control positioning.

text: Specialization Reassignment Initial choice — Level 3. Choose one Specialization available to your class. Reassignment checkpoints — Levels 6, 10, and 14. When gaining one of these levels, you may either continue your current Specialization or change to another Specialization available to your class. If you change Specialization, remove every feature granted by the previous Specialization and replace it with the complete feature package of the newly selected Specialization through your current checkpoint . Features from different Specializations cannot be mixed, retained, or combined. When newly entering a Specialization, make any choices required by the features you now gain. Continuing the same Specialization does not reset earlier internal choices unless an explicit feature says otherwise. If the removed Specialization granted extra known options, selections, capacities, or Specialization-dependent maxima, remove, reselect, or recalculate them as necessary to satisfy the new path. Reassignment itself does not restore HP or class resources, and current values cannot remain above any new maximum. Reassignment occurs only as part of gaining Level 6, Level 10, or Level 14 . It cannot be performed through a rest, downtime, training, ordinary retraining, or between adventures. The Level 14 decision is the final normal Specialization choice and remains locked through Level 20 unless a later explicit rule says otherwise.

text: Spell Acquisition Spells are class-granted abilities. They cannot be bought, sold, looted, copied from spellbooks or scrolls, learned from vendors, or acquired by commerce or exploration. A spell becomes available only when the character reaches its Unlock Level and, when applicable, satisfies the immediately preceding spell in its linear prerequisite chain. Unlocking a later spell never removes the earlier spell. Newly unlocked spells begin at Spell Level 1 unless explicitly stated otherwise. Spell Advancement — Final Rule. A class grants Spell Advancements according to its finalized progression. One Spell Advancement raises one eligible unlocked spell by 1 Spell Level, subject to that class’s Maximum Spell Level and listed prerequisites. Unspent Spell Advancements may be banked indefinitely, but banked or newly earned Spell Advancements may be spent only when the character gains a level; they cannot normally be spent during an adventure, between encounters, or during a rest. A character cannot spend more Spell Advancements than they have earned. Spell Retraining. There is no universal spell retraining. Once a Spell Advancement is spent, it is permanent unless a specific class feature, explicit story effect, or GM-approved exceptional circumstance directly permits reassignment.

title: Spell Advancement & Reading Spell Entries
desc: Spell Level is permanent mastery of an individual spell; casting frequency controls how often that spell can be used. Spell Advancements are spent only at allowed level-up timing, and linear prerequisites apply where listed. The complete individual spell entries follow immediately in Part VIII of this handbook.

title: Spell Resolution Rules
desc: Spell Attacks and Saves. Spell Attack = Proficiency Bonus + the class’s spellcasting ability modifier. Spell Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + that ability modifier. Sorcerer, Spiritmaster, and Chanter use Intelligence; Cleric uses Wisdom; Songweaver uses Charisma for spells. Class features that use another ability retain their own rule. Effect-Removal Check
text: Spell Resolution Rules Spell Attacks and Saves. Spell Attack = Proficiency Bonus + the class’s spellcasting ability modifier. Spell Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + that ability modifier. Sorcerer, Spiritmaster, and Chanter use Intelligence; Cleric uses Wisdom; Songweaver uses Charisma for spells. Class features that use another ability retain their own rule. Effect-Removal Check DC. When Aether Dispel, a Cleric Purification Check, or another effect explicitly calls for a check against a hostile magical or removable effect’s DC, use that effect’s listed save DC, removal DC, or feature DC when one exists. If no applicable DC is listed, use DC 15. A spell that supplies its own different DC uses that value. Successfully Affect. For hostile spell interactions, a spell Successfully Affects a creature if the creature takes damage, is hit, fails a save, or suffers a meaningful hostile Condition, penalty, forced movement, or other combat effect. Harmless targeting, immunity, or an effect that changes nothing does not count. Area Resolution. Unless stated otherwise, each creature in an area rolls its own save once per application. A creature is affected only if its space intersects the spell area and Line of Effect exists. Cover and Line of Effect. Half Cover applies normally to spell attacks and Dexterity saving throws. Full Cover blocks the relevant Line of Effect and therefore blocks the spell unless the spell explicitly says otherwise. Origin, range, and Cover are measured from the caster unless a class feature explicitly changes the origin. Self-Range Projection. A Self-range spell cannot be projected from another creature or Spirit unless a rule explicitly allows it. Critical Hits. When a spell attack critically hits, double all damage dice rolled as part of that attack, including direct spell riders. Independent later damage, zones, damage-over-time ticks, and separate trap or Spirit effects do not double unless explicitly part of the Critical Hit. Damage-over-Time and Repeated Zones. A creature normally takes a spell’s repeated damage no more than once per turn from that casting unless the spell explicitly says otherwise. A creature cannot repeatedly enter and leave the same area during one turn to multiply a once-per-turn effect. Suppression vs. Ending. Ending a spell removes it. Suppression pauses its mechanics while its duration continues. When suppression ends, the spell resumes if duration remains. Stacking. Multiple copies of the same named spell on the same creature do not stack unless the spell says otherwise; use the strongest applicable numeric effect. Different named spells stack unless a class or global rule says they do not. Flat class-feature save or attack penalties do not stack unless explicitly stated. Cooldown Terminology. The legacy term “1-Round Cooldown” means Cooldown 2: after use, the spell is unavailable on the caster’s next turn and becomes available again on the following turn. A class feature that permits an At-Will or 1-Round-Cooldown spell therefore permits an eligible, currently available Cooldown 2 spell; it does not permit Cooldown 3 unless explicitly stated. Restoration of Uses. Short-Rest-limited spells recover after a completed Short or Long Rest. Long-Rest-limited spells recover only after a Long Rest. A rest cannot be repeatedly interrupted or manufactured solely to farm uses contrary to genuine play. NPCs and Monsters. NPC and monster spell-like abilities may use simplified statblock recharge rules. Player spell-access and Spell Advancement rules apply only to player-class spellcasting unless a creature explicitly uses a player class.

title: Spellcasting
desc: Does Wings of Atreia use spell slots or cantrips? No. There are no spell slots and no cantrip category. Each spell has its own frequency: At-Will, Cooldown, Short Rest, or Long Rest. Does ordinary damage force a Concentration save? No. Ordinary damage does not test Concentration. Concentration ends only according to the Wings of Atreia Concentration rules an
text: Spellcasting Does Wings of Atreia use spell slots or cantrips? No. There are no spell slots and no cantrip category. Each spell has its own frequency: At-Will, Cooldown, Short Rest, or Long Rest. Does ordinary damage force a Concentration save? No. Ordinary damage does not test Concentration. Concentration ends only according to the Wings of Atreia Concentration rules and explicit effects. Can I buy, copy, or learn spells from scrolls? Not as a universal rule. Spells are class-granted and unlock through class progression and their printed prerequisites. Does every Spell Advancement make the spell mechanically stronger? No. One Spell Advancement raises one eligible unlocked spell by exactly +1 Spell Level . A Spell Level is not automatically a mechanical improvement breakpoint. If the new Spell Level is not listed in that spell's Spell-Level Scaling or Milestone Improvements , record the higher Spell Level normally but do not change damage, healing, range, area, duration, riders, or any other effect. Do not invent compensation. The progression-only Spell Level remains valid permanent progression, may satisfy prerequisites, and counts toward the next listed improvement. Can I skip an unexciting Spell Level and jump to the next improvement? No. Each Spell Advancement increases the selected eligible spell by exactly one Spell Level. Progression-only levels are still real levels. Does casting a Bonus Action spell prevent me from casting another spell that turn? No universal D&D-style Bonus Action spell restriction exists. Follow the actual Action/Bonus Action timing and the individual spell text.

text: Spirit Bond Spirit Bond begins at 0 when genuine combat starts and resets to 0 when combat ends. Maximum Bond is 3 at Level 1, 4 at Level 2, 5 at Level 5, and 6 at Level 9; Bondweaver increases this maximum by 1 from Level 3 onward. Once on each of your turns, gain 1 Spirit Bond if both you and your spirit successfully affect hostile creatures during that turn. Successfully Affect means damage, a hit, a failed save, meaningful hostile condition/penalty, forced movement, or another real combat effect. Merely targeting or applying an effect to which the target is immune does not count. Independent riders do not recursively generate Bond.

title: Spiritmaster
desc: Complete player reference for the Spiritmaster class in Wings of Atreia, based on Player Handbook v3.10.
text: Full Caster • Elemental Spirit • Spirit Bond • Debuffs Spiritmaster “Never fight alone. Your spirit is with you.” Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. This page preserves the handbook's class material and ordering. Spellcasting Reference: Spiritmaster has a dedicated spell-list page for quick browsing. View Spiritmaster Spell List → Class Identity Class Chassis Core Engine — Summon Spirit Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Spell List Specializations Preview Level 1–20 Action & Resource Reference Level-by-Level Progression Example Combat Sequence Specialization Reassignment The Spiritmaster is a two-body tactical caster. One active elemental spirit shares the Spiritmaster’s turn and action economy; together they equal one complete player character. The class establishes two battlefield positions, casts through the spirit, and earns Spirit Bond only through meaningful master-spirit coordination. Class Identity Spiritmasters are binders and commanders of elemental spirits who fight as a partnership rather than as a solitary caster. Their strength comes from coordinating their own spellcraft with a Greater Spirit, applying pressure, disruption, and control across more than one position on the battlefield. Spirit Bond represents the relationship and command structure that makes this divided presence function as one class. Tradition & Outlook The Spiritmaster tradition develops from Atreia’s mage disciplines but turns outward toward spirits, elemental forces, and the difficult art of directing entities shaped by Aether. Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power. Appearance & Adventuring Spiritmasters use cloth armor and magical implements, while the visible presence of a summoned spirit often defines their silhouette more strongly than clothing does. Their equipment may include ritual, scholarly, or elemental motifs without creating additional mechanics. They adventure to understand unusual spirits, recover lost summoning knowledge, counter supernatural threats, serve as versatile magical operatives, or deepen the bond between Daeva and elemental ally. Only one Spiritmaster spirit may normally be active. Summoning uses an Action and places the spirit in a visible unoccupied space within 15 feet. A defeated spirit disperses into Aether, makes no death saves, and cannot be resummoned until the start of your next turn. Outside combat a newly summoned spirit appears at full HP; voluntary replacement during combat preserves the dismissed spirit’s current HP percentage rather than healing by switching forms. Successfully Affect means damage, a hit, a failed save, meaningful hostile condition/penalty, forced movement, or another real combat effect. Merely targeting or applying an effect to which the target is immune does not count. Independent riders do not recursively generate Bond. text: Targeting and Valid Targets Legal wording. An effect can affect only a target permitted by its text. Range. Check range when the effect is used. Line of Effect. Normally required unless the effect says otherwise. “Can see.” Requires both visibility and a valid unobstructed line for the effect. Unseen target. Use the base unseen-attacker/target procedure. If you attack a creature you cannot see but whose location you know, the attack has Disadvantage. If its location is unknown, you must first choose the space you are attacking; the attack automatically misses if the creature is not there. A spell requiring 'a creature you can see' cannot target an unseen creature. Self. “A creature” may include the user unless the text says “another creature.” Objects. Cannot be targeted by creature-only effects. Invalid target. An obvious invalid target caused by a rules misunderstanding does not normally waste the Action; hidden invalidity can still consume it at GM discretion. Choose. Means deliberate selection; it does not imply accidental targets.

title: Templar
desc: Complete player reference for the Templar class in Wings of Atreia, based on Player Handbook v3.10.
text: Martial Defender • Resolve • Challenge • Interception Templar “You're only as good as your armor.” The premier martial defender, turning incoming pressure into protection, damage reduction, retaliation, and formation control. Website rules source: Wings of Atreia Player Handbook v3.10 — Publication Master, 8 September 2026. Overview Class Chassis Resolve Signature Mechanics Action Reference Specializations Preview Levels 1–20 Defensive Examples Specialization Reassignment Class Overview The Templar is the system’s premier martial defender. It does not force enemies to attack it through mind control; instead, Challenge makes ignoring the Templar tactically dangerous while Resolve turns incoming pressure into protection, damage reduction, retaliation, and formation control. Class Identity Templars are guardian-warriors whose strength is measured by what they can endure and whom they can keep standing. They occupy the most dangerous space in a battle, challenge enemies that would otherwise overwhelm vulnerable allies, and turn personal resilience into protection for the group. Resolve is the mechanical expression of this identity: a Templar grows most meaningful when danger is real and protection requires commitment. Tradition & Outlook The Templar tradition grows from Atreia’s warrior disciplines but places duty, discipline, guardianship, and control above personal glory. Templars are found among legion defenders, fortress guardians, sworn protectors, escorts, and Daevas who believe power carries an obligation to stand between danger and others. Individual Templars may be stern, compassionate, devout, pragmatic, or fiercely patriotic, but the class ideal is constancy under pressure. Appearance & Adventuring Templars are commonly associated with plate armor, shields, and the unmistakable silhouette of a heavily protected frontline Daeva. Their equipment tends to emphasize readiness and endurance rather than ornament alone. Templars adventure because someone must hold the line: to defend a community, fulfill an oath, guard companions, reclaim threatened territory, or confront enemies that cannot safely be allowed to reach the rest of the party. Class Chassis Trait Rule Primary Class Ability Constitution Weapon Ability Strength Hit Die d12 Hit Points at Level 1 16 + CON modifier Hit Points at Higher Levels Roll d12 or use fixed 7, add CON modifier, then add +4 maximum HP from Templar durability each Templar level after 1. Saving Throws Strength, Constitution Armor Chain Armor, Plate Armor, Round/Medium/Tower Shields Weapons Longswords, Polearms, Maces Class Save DC 8 + PB + CON modifier Signature Resource Resolve Signature Mechanics Resolute Guard, Challenge, Guardian’s Intercession Extra Attack Level 5; two attacks only Spellcasting None Core Engine — Resolve Resolve represents the Templar converting battlefield pressure into defensive certainty. Unless a later feature states otherwise, Resolve becomes 0 when Initiative is rolled, becomes 0 when combat ends, and cannot be gained while you are Incapacitated. Hold the Line: gain 1 Resolve when a hostile creature you can see hits you with an attack while you are within that creature’s melee reach. Protect the Vulnerable: gain 1 Resolve when a Templar class feature successfully reduces, prevents, redirects, or intercepts damage that would otherwise be dealt to another creature, or when a feature explicitly says the protection qualifies. Defy the Templar: gain 1 Resolve when a creature Challenged by you attacks another creature while you were a valid target for that attack. You can normally gain no more than 1 Resolve during any creature’s turn. One event grants Resolve only once even if it satisfies multiple triggers. Maximum Resolve: 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–14; 6 at 15–20. Resource Flow — Generation, Recovery, Spending & Reset Resource Flow Rule Starting State Resolve normally becomes 0 when Initiative is rolled. Later Templar features explicitly establish starting Resolve. Maximum 3 at Levels 1–4; 4 at 5–8; 5 at 9–14; 6 at 15–20. How You Gain It Hold the Line, Protect the Vulnerable, and Defy the Templar. Generation Limits Normally no more than 1 Resolve during any creature’s turn. One event grants Resolve only once even if it satisfies multiple triggers. No Resolve while Incapacitated. How You Spend It Resolute Guard 1; Guardian’s Rally 1; Bulwark Shared Resolve 1; Resolute Shelter 1; Bulwark Last Wall 1; Refuse to Fall 3. Other features spend Resolve only when their text states a cost. Same-Trigger Timing When a protection feature both resolves and legitimately generates Resolve, newly gained Resolve can pay an eligible same-trigger defensive technique when the feature permits the timing. Reset Resolve becomes 0 when combat ends. Resolve Timing Rules Resolve from Hold the Line may immediately be spent on Resolute Guard against the same triggering attack’s damage. Resolve generated by a successful Guardian’s Intercession is gained before redirected damage is applied, so it may be used against the redirected attack if otherwise legal. Resolve generated because Guardian’s Shelter changed a save from failure to success may immediately pay for Resolute Shelter at Level 14. Challenge may remain on a creature while its penalty is temporarily suppressed because you are out of range, cannot be perceived, or are not a legal target. Signature Defensive Mechanics Resolute Guard When you take damage from an attack, spend 1 Resolve with no action required to reduce that damage by 1 Guard Die + your CON modifier, minimum 0. The Guard Die is d6 at Level 1, d8 from Level 5, d10 from Level 9, and d12 from Level 15. You can normally use Resolute Guard only once per turn unless a Templar feature explicitly says otherwise. Challenge As a Bonus Action, choose one hostile creature you can see within 30 feet. It is Challenged until the start of your next turn. Initially you can maintain one Challenge. While the creature is within 30 feet, can perceive you, and you are a valid target for at least one attack it could make, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures other than you. Challenge is nonmagical, has no save, and is neither Charm nor Fear. Guardian’s Intercession When an ally within 5 feet is hit by an attack, use your Reaction to redirect that attack to yourself. Use the same attack roll. If it hits your AC, you take the attack and its damage/effects normally; if it misses your AC, the redirected attack misses. A successful interception qualifies for Protect the Vulnerable when it actually prevents the ally from receiving the attack’s damage. text: Tempo Tempo is a genuine-combat resource representing firing rhythm, accuracy, and momentum. It begins at 0, resets to 0 when combat ends, and artificial initiative cannot generate it. text: Territorial Familiarity Territorial Familiarity applies only while you are within territory currently controlled by your own faction. It represents practical familiarity with ordinary faction-held settlements, routes, public landmarks, infrastructure, and commonly available local information. It does not grant automatic Advantage, does not automatically reveal hidden or secret information, and creates no combat bonus. When relevant, Territorial Familiarity can justify ordinary narrative knowledge or permission to attempt a local-knowledge check that would not be reasonable for an outsider. Examples include recognizing a commonly used route, knowing where a public service or landmark is normally found, or understanding routine faction infrastructure. The GM still decides whether a check is needed and which Ability or Skill applies. Familiarity never supplies information your faction could not reasonably possess. ← Back to Rules

title: The Abyss Opens
desc: Between Elysea and Asmodae lay the shattered space known as Reshanta—the Abyss . What had separated the two realms also became a path between them: a vast and dangerous expanse of floating land, ruined places, unstable space, and strategic positions unlike anything found in the lands below. When Elyos and Asmodian forces began entering the Abyss, they encoun
text: The Abyss Opens Between Elysea and Asmodae lay the shattered space known as Reshanta—the Abyss . What had separated the two realms also became a path between them: a vast and dangerous expanse of floating land, ruined places, unstable space, and strategic positions unlike anything found in the lands below. When Elyos and Asmodian forces began entering the Abyss, they encountered one another again. Centuries of separation had not prepared either side for reconciliation. Suspicion became confrontation, and confrontation became battle. The Abyss offered routes, fortresses, resources, and control over the space between worlds. Neither side was willing to surrender it to the other.

title: The Cataclysm
desc: The final crisis around the Tower ended not with the restoration of the old world, but with disaster. The Tower of Eternity was shattered. Atreia broke apart, and the world that had once been whole was divided into two great surviving realms. The Tower Guardians, Siel and Israphel , stood at the heart of that terrible moment. Their actions became part of the
text: The Cataclysm The final crisis around the Tower ended not with the restoration of the old world, but with disaster. The Tower of Eternity was shattered. Atreia broke apart, and the world that had once been whole was divided into two great surviving realms. The Tower Guardians, Siel and Israphel , stood at the heart of that terrible moment. Their actions became part of the history and legend surrounding the world's survival, even as the Cataclysm ended the age of a united Atreia. From that point forward, the survivors of the north and south would rebuild separately.

title: The First Phase of the Abyss War
desc: The conflict in the Abyss did not remain a war between two peoples. The Balaur were there as well, turning the struggle into a three-sided war in which yesterday's battlefield could become tomorrow's fortress and no victory could be assumed permanent. The Elyos established their foothold at Terminon . The Asmodians held Primum . Beyond them, Balaur power rem
text: The First Phase of the Abyss War The conflict in the Abyss did not remain a war between two peoples. The Balaur were there as well, turning the struggle into a three-sided war in which yesterday's battlefield could become tomorrow's fortress and no victory could be assumed permanent. The Elyos established their foothold at Terminon . The Asmodians held Primum . Beyond them, Balaur power remained entrenched across the greater Abyss. Daevas now took to the air not merely to explore the shattered realm, but to fight for it. Elyos. Asmodians. Balaur. Three powers contest the Abyss, each with its own purpose, history, and claim upon the future of Atreia. This is the age into which newly Ascended Daevas spread their wings. This player history ends at the opening campaign era. What comes next belongs to the story at the table.

title: The Millennium War
desc: The struggle against the Balaur became a war measured not in seasons, but in generations. As the conflict deepened, extraordinary Daevas were elevated into the Twelve Empyrean Lords , champions whose power and leadership became central to Atreia's resistance. The war changed societies, hardened loyalties, and placed the Tower of Eternity itself at the center
text: The Millennium War The struggle against the Balaur became a war measured not in seasons, but in generations. As the conflict deepened, extraordinary Daevas were elevated into the Twelve Empyrean Lords , champions whose power and leadership became central to Atreia's resistance. The war changed societies, hardened loyalties, and placed the Tower of Eternity itself at the center of Atreia's fate. Eventually, the desperate search for an end to the conflict led to events that would reshape the world forever.

title: The Rise of the Balaur
desc: Among the ancient Drakan, one rose beyond the limits of his kind: Fregion . Elevated by Aion for his exceptional nature, Fregion became the first of what would later be known as the Dragon Lords. In time, Fregion discovered Id and drew upon a power beyond the ordinary strength of the Drakan. Through that power, other exceptional Drakans were raised into Drag
text: The Rise of the Balaur Among the ancient Drakan, one rose beyond the limits of his kind: Fregion . Elevated by Aion for his exceptional nature, Fregion became the first of what would later be known as the Dragon Lords. In time, Fregion discovered Id and drew upon a power beyond the ordinary strength of the Drakan. Through that power, other exceptional Drakans were raised into Dragon Lords. Under their rule, the old Drakan order transformed into the power remembered and feared as the Balaur . Their growing strength brought them into catastrophic conflict with the rest of Atreia.

title: Theft and Pickpocket

If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the t
text: Theft and Pickpocket A theft attempt requires a plausible opportunity. Taking an accessible small item uses Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against Passive Perception and must exceed it. If the target is actively watching, oppose with active Perception; ties favor the observer. Secured items can require a different approach. Failure may create suspicion or alarm. Success means the theft was unnoticed at that moment; later discovery remains possible. Distraction creates opportunity rather than automatic success. Help can grant +2 when genuinely meaningful. Worn armor, shields, Wings, wielded weapons, and equipped mandatory implements cannot simply be pickpocketed. Repeated attempts require changed circumstances.

title: Theobomos
desc: Theobomos is a scorched and devastated eastern island whose landscape bears wounds that ordinary weather and time have not erased. Ruins, archaeological sites, burned terrain, and supernatural scars make it one of Elysea’s clearest reminders that the wars of Atreia can permanently change the land. The region is not simply empty destruction; expeditions, rese
text: Theobomos Theobomos is a scorched and devastated eastern island whose landscape bears wounds that ordinary weather and time have not erased. Ruins, archaeological sites, burned terrain, and supernatural scars make it one of Elysea’s clearest reminders that the wars of Atreia can permanently change the land. The region is not simply empty destruction; expeditions, researchers, soldiers, and those reclaiming knowledge still have reasons to enter it. Its damaged environment gives every surviving structure and recovered record unusual weight. Daevas come to Theobomos to investigate the past, secure dangerous sites, recover history, and confront threats that flourish in devastated ground. Archaeology here is rarely a quiet academic exercise, because ancient remains can intersect with hostile forces, unstable conditions, and the consequences of old battles. The region supports adventures that make history physically present rather than something confined to books. For Elyos characters, Theobomos is both a warning and a challenge: devastation happened here, yet the story of the land is not finished.

text: Tradition & Outlook Aethertech is a comparatively modern Daeva discipline born from the recovery, study, and weaponization of advanced magical technology. The wider Aion tradition connects the class to Daeva analysis of Danuar technology and the lessons surrounding Hyperion; Wings of Atreia preserves that technological identity while its own campaign chronology and mechanics remain authoritative. Aethertechs often value ingenuity, technical discipline, experimentation, and the belief that knowledge taken from dangerous enemies can be turned toward Atreia’s defense.

text: Tradition & Outlook The Assassin tradition descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines and is practiced by infiltrators, covert operatives, hunters of dangerous individuals, intelligence agents, and Daevas who favor certainty over spectacle. Assassins often prize patience, awareness, self-control, and economy of motion. Their motives vary widely: service to a faction, revenge, professional duty, protection through preemptive action, or the pursuit of perfect technique.

Chanters are often teachers, battle companions, spiritual guides, martial ascetics, or morale-keepers. text: Tradition & Outlook The Cleric tradition grows from Atreia’s priestly disciplines and is associated with healers, battlefield ministers, temple servants, protectors of communities, and Daevas who understand survival as a collective responsibility. text: Tradition & Outlook The Gladiator tradition descends from the broad warrior disciplines of Atreia and is associated with soldiers, arena fighters, legion veterans, weapon masters, and Daevas who believe that skill must survive contact with a real battlefield. Gladiators commonly value courage, physical discipline, adaptability, and decisive action. Some fight for glory or personal mastery; others see themselves as the hard edge of a legion, the Daeva who advances when everyone else needs the line to move.

text: Tradition & Outlook Gunslingers belong to Atreia’s newer technological traditions. Gunslingers often value nerve, technical familiarity, accuracy, independence, and adaptability.

text: Tradition & Outlook The Ranger tradition also descends from Atreia’s scout disciplines, but where Assassins close with a chosen target, Rangers cultivate distance, fieldcraft, and control of the approach. text: Tradition & Outlook The Sorcerer tradition grows from Atreia’s mage disciplines and is associated with formal magical study, experimentation, academies, battlefield arcanists, and Daevas fascinated by the structure of Aether itself. Sorcerers commonly value knowledge, precision, preparation, and intellectual mastery, although their personalities range from scholarly restraint to spectacular confidence. For many, magic is both a weapon and a language through which Atreia can be understood.

Spiritmasters are often patient observers, researchers, summoners, or specialists in threats that cannot be understood through ordinary physical study. Their beliefs about spirits differ: some emphasize command, others partnership, responsibility, curiosity, or respect for elemental power.

text: Tradition & Outlook The Templar tradition grows from Atreia’s warrior disciplines but places duty, discipline, guardianship, and control above personal glory. Templars are found among legion defenders, fortress guardians, sworn protectors, escorts, and Daevas who believe power carries an obligation to stand between danger and others. Individual Templars may be stern, compassionate, devout, pragmatic, or fiercely patriotic, but the class ideal is constancy under pressure.

text: Traps and Non-Aether Hazards Describe a hazard with Trigger, Detection, Avoid/Disable method, Save/Check, Effect, and Reset/Duration. Hazards may be obvious, concealed, or hidden. Detection normally uses Passive Perception, active Perception, or Investigation.
